More than 15,000 souls were left homeless and seven were injured in the wake of an overnight fire that engulfed a slum area. The flames, born in a humble shanty house in the district of Tondo, quickly spread like a hungry beast, devouring everything in its path. Senior Superintendent Wilfredo Tiu, a regional chief of the Bureau of Fire Protection, recounted the harrowing scene as 1,200 shanty houses were reduced to ash over the course of 10 long hours. Amidst the chaos, brave residents risked life and limb to salvage their possessions before fleeing the encroaching inferno. As dawn broke over the smoldering ruins, three evacuation centers opened their doors to offer solace to the 3,000 families who had lost everything. The air was thick with the acrid scent of smoke, and the wails of the displaced filled the air as they clung to the few belongings they managed to salvage. Despite the valiant efforts of firefighters, the aftermath of the blaze was a stark reminder of the fragility of life in the city's impoverished corners. As investigators combed through the wreckage to determine the fire's cause, the specter of faulty electrical wiring loomed large, a grim reminder of the precarious conditions that many in the slum area called home.

A series of explosions disrupted a procession by Shiite Muslims in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, resulting in the death of at least one individual and injuring numerous others, some of whom sustained serious injuries. The incident occurred on the holy day of Ashura, as reported by the police. The explosions were caused by improvised explosive devices, according to the authorities, and the perpetrators of the attack remain unidentified. A hospital official confirmed that at least 10 of the wounded individuals were admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for treatment. While attacks against the Shiite minority in Bangladesh have been uncommon, the country is predominantly Sunni Muslim. However, recent events, including the claimed responsibility by the Islamic State group for the killings of an Italian aid worker and a Japanese man, as well as previous attacks on secular bloggers, have heightened concerns regarding security in the region.

In James Lydon's masterful work, "The Making of Ireland," readers are taken on a captivating journey through the intricate tapestry of Irish history. With vivid prose and meticulous attention to detail, Lydon vividly paints a picture of the diverse waves of settlers, missionaries, and invaders that have shaped the Emerald Isle since time immemorial. From the arrival of St. Patrick in the fifth century to the tumultuous encounters with Henry II and beyond, Lydon skillfully weaves together the threads of Ireland's past to illuminate its present. Through his exploration of the ever-changing racial landscape and the enduring struggle with England, Lydon unveils the complex political and cultural forces that continue to define Ireland today. "The Making of Ireland" stands as a testament to Lydon's expertise and passion for history, offering readers a compelling and comprehensive narrative that is as enlightening as it is engaging.

Ben Murdoch-Masila's electrifying performances at the World Cup have not gone unnoticed, with NRL clubs vying for his signature. The powerful forward, known affectionately as "BMM", has been a force to be reckoned with for Tonga, showcasing the same brilliance that earned him accolades in the Super League. The Gold Coast have expressed interest in bringing him back to Australia, igniting hope for fans eager to see him in action once again. As he prepares for the pivotal clash against England, Murdoch-Masila's determination and passion are palpable, fueling his desire to make a lasting impact on the rugby league world. The prospect of a return to the NRL brings a new sense of excitement and purpose to his already illustrious career, and fans can't help but feel a surge of anticipation for what the future holds for this dynamic player.

The Tel Aviv municipal building stood tall and proud, its facade adorned with the Egyptian flag as a poignant gesture of solidarity with our neighbors in their time of sorrow. As the clock struck 11:00pm on that Saturday evening, a somber hush fell over the city, a silent tribute to the 29 lives lost in a senseless act of violence. The colored lights, so often used to celebrate joyous occasions, now shone in a different hue, a symbol of unity and support for the grieving Egyptian people and Coptic Christians.

In a city where symbols of pride and solidarity are not uncommon, this display held a special significance - it was the first time an Arab nation's flag graced the iconic landmark, a poignant reminder of the bonds that transcend borders and differences. The brutal attack on innocent Copts on their way to a monastery in Minya sent shockwaves through the region, prompting a swift and heartfelt response from the Arab world and beyond.

As the details of the attack emerged, the horror and senselessness of it all became painfully clear. Masked gunmen, claiming allegiance to ISIS, had targeted and mercilessly killed dozens of Coptic Christians, leaving a trail of devastation in their wake. The toll of 29 lives lost, the innocent victims branded as "crusaders" by their heartless assailants, served as a stark reminder of the profound suffering and fear faced by minority communities in the region.

Amidst the darkness of this tragedy, the light of solidarity and compassion shone brightly. The outpouring of condolences and support from around the world was a testament to the shared humanity that binds us all. As Coptic Christians in Egypt continued to face threats and violence from extremist groups, the need for unity and resilience became more urgent than ever.

In this moment of reflection and remembrance, let us hold in our hearts the memory of those who lost their lives and the resilience of those who continue to stand strong in the face of adversity. Let us stand together, hand in hand, as a testament to the enduring power of love and compassion in the face of hatred and violence.

On Wednesday morning, a heartfelt tribute was held for 23-year-old Danyelle Luckey, a young woman who tragically lost her life while serving her country. The "Military Escort Team" solemnly led the procession as Luckey's casket arrived at Solomon Temple Missionary Baptist Church. Nearly two hundred individuals gathered to bid farewell to the Pittsburg native, who had bravely joined the Navy in pursuit of a brighter future for herself and her loved ones. Her selfless goal was to save money to send her young nephew to college. As the family arrived at the church, Luckey's father made a poignant gesture by wearing his daughter's fatigues, a touching tribute to her service. Luckey passed away while on duty aboard an aircraft carrier in the Philippine Sea. She fell ill one day, retired to her bunk to rest, and tragically never awoke. The Navy has determined that Luckey suffered from cardiac arrest, however, her passing remains under investigation. The family has shared that an autopsy is currently being conducted, with results expected in the coming weeks.

Your spare blanket or stored winter clothing may be taking up more closet space than necessary due to the excess air that fills them out and gives them bulk. By vacuum-sealing your belongings, you can efficiently reduce them to their minimum sizes without causing any damage. Contrary to what expensive storage bags marketed for this purpose may suggest, you can achieve the same result using household items you already have. Simply fold the clothes, blankets, or other items you plan to store, and place them neatly inside a sturdy trash bag. By inserting the hose attachment of a vacuum cleaner into the bag and gradually removing the air, you can easily free up closet or suitcase space. This DIY method not only protects your belongings from the elements but also saves you money on unnecessary storage solutions.

The initial phase of the project to enhance bike lanes and reduce vehicle lanes along Folsom Street in Boulder has been successfully completed. Known as the "right-sizing" initiative by Boulder transportation planners, this pilot project aims to assess the impact of wider, protected bike lanes on increasing cycling rates, as well as the effects on vehicle travel times and accident rates with a shift to one lane of travel in each direction accompanied by a center turn lane. While reducing vehicle lanes was necessary to accommodate the expanded bike lanes, the addition of a center turn lane is expected to mitigate accidents and minimize disruptions to travel times, as it prevents cars from rear-ending or getting stuck behind left-turning vehicles. Recent developments include the installation of new bike lanes with a striped buffer along Folsom Street, spanning from Valmont Road to Canyon Boulevard, transitioning from two lanes in each direction to one lane each way with a central turn lane. In the upcoming days, green markings within the buffer zone and flexible bollards for added delineation of the bike lane will be implemented. Furthermore, similar street enhancements are planned for Iris Avenue in late August, followed by the commencement of work on 63rd Street in September.

Pakistan's military has reported that it has successfully eliminated at least 910 suspected militants since commencing an offensive in the tribal area of North Waziristan in June. The statement also noted that 82 soldiers had lost their lives while combating the insurgents in North Waziristan and during raids across the country. The army declared that it now has control over the main towns in North Waziristan, previously a stronghold for the Taliban. However, media access is restricted in tribal areas near the Afghan border, and there is no independent verification of the military's claims. The release of the army's statement coincides with escalating anti-government protests in the capital, with the military emphasizing that it is not taking sides in the crisis. The offensive against the Pakistani Taliban was launched following the breakdown of peace talks between the militants and the government. The military's statement highlighted that major towns in North Waziristan, including Miranshah, Mir Ali, Datta Khel, Boya, and Degan, have been cleared of terrorists. The army also reported that 42 militants were killed in intelligence-led operations across the country, with over 100 others captured. However, no civilian casualties were detailed, despite reports from displaced residents suggesting otherwise. The ongoing conflict has forced approximately 800,000 people to flee their homes in North Waziristan since June, with a noticeable decrease in militant attacks within Pakistan since the commencement of the offensive. Nevertheless, no high-profile militant leaders have been apprehended thus far, with the military acknowledging in July that many may have escaped North Waziristan after being forewarned of the impending military action.

Leeds United is poised to extend an invitation to Nile Ranger, as Sky Sports has learned. The 23-year-old, currently without a club after parting ways with Swindon Town, has been plagued by disciplinary issues and off-field troubles. Despite his tumultuous journey since his professional debut five years ago, Ranger's potential has not gone unnoticed. Sources reveal that Leeds' head coach Dave Hockaday and his assistant Junior Lewis are considering the possibility of bringing Ranger in for training in the near future, with the potential of offering him a contract. Ranger, a former England youth international, showcased his prowess by netting seven goals in just 19 appearances for Swindon last season.

There is a certain magic in naming a cloud, as it gives it a personality and a sense of familiarity. Hector, the formidable thunderstorm complex that reigns over the Tiwi Islands, holds a special place in the hearts of those who study the intricacies of tropical meteorology. Its daily appearance during the months of Nov-Dec and Feb-March is a reliable spectacle, a reminder of nature's raw power and beauty. The sheer magnitude of Hector, with its towering height of 20km and the energy of ten Hiroshima-sized bombs, is enough to leave anyone in awe. To witness its majestic presence from afar, casting a shadow over Darwin, is a humbling experience. It is fitting that the locals have bestowed such a fearsome entity with a name that exudes strength and character. Thank you, Tim Garrett, for capturing the essence of Hector in your photos.

Animata is a real-time animation software that is open source and specifically designed for creating animations and interactive background projections for concerts, theatre, and dance performances. One of the unique features of this software is its ability to generate animations in real-time, allowing for continuous interaction. This feature also enables the integration of physical sensors, cameras, or other environmental variables to control the animation of characters, resulting in cartoons that can react to their surroundings. For instance, users can easily create a virtual puppet band that responds to live audio input or set up a scene with drawn characters controlled by the movements of dancers. Unlike traditional 3D animation programs, Animata simplifies the process of creating characters, requiring just a few minutes. By utilizing still images as the skeleton for puppets, a network of triangles is created and linked with a bone structure. The movement of these bones is governed by a physical model, facilitating easy manipulation of the characters.

After a several year hiatus, the African-American Parade of Connecticut made a triumphant return on Saturday, breathing new life into the streets of Hartford. The atmosphere crackled with excitement and anticipation, as vibrant floats and lively music set the stage for a celebration like no other. The crowd buzzed with energy, their faces beaming with pride and joy as they eagerly awaited the start of the procession. However, amidst the sea of positivity, a jarring discordance cut through the air in the form of negative chanting from a political campaign, an unwelcome intrusion in the otherwise harmonious atmosphere.

The staging area, a mere block from Walnut to Albany on Edwards, teemed with activity as participants readied themselves for the grand spectacle. Colorful vehicles adorned the parade route, their gleaming exteriors a testament to the pride and dedication of their owners. An air of anticipation hung heavy in the air as police officers stood vigilant, ensuring the smooth flow of the event by pausing motor vehicle traffic during the parade.

With a burst of energy, the parade kicked off from the corner of Edwards and Albany, setting the streets ablaze with its infectious enthusiasm. It snaked its way up the avenue, the procession weaving a tapestry of cultural pride and unity as it turned down Woodland and made its way to the grand finale in Keney Park. Here, the festivities continued with Family Day activities, a vibrant tapestry of community spirit and togetherness that would linger in the hearts of all who attended.

A diverse array of participants lent their unique flair to the festivities, each group adding their own special touch to the kaleidoscope of colors and sounds. From the spirited Weaver High cheerleaders to the solemn presence of religious organizations, from the sleek motorcycles of a dedicated club to the impassioned voices of the NAACP, the parade was a melting pot of cultural richness and unity. Even campaigning politicians joined in, adding their voices to the symphony of celebration.

As the parade wove its way through the heart of Hartford, it became a living, breathing testament to the resilience and vibrancy of the African-American community in Connecticut. It was a day of joy, of unity, and of pride, a day that would be etched in the memories of all who bore witness to its magic.

Almost 18 years after the tragic explosion of Trans World Airlines Flight 800, the mystery surrounding the crash continues to captivate and intrigue. Was it terrorism, missiles, or even a secret microwave weapon that brought down the Boeing 747? Despite extensive investigations by the FBI and the NTSB, questions remain unanswered and conspiracy theories persist. Some believe the plane was struck by missiles, while others suggest a terrorist bomb was the cause. And then there's the outlandish theory of a microwave weapon targeting the aircraft. A recent documentary shed light on these alternate theories, but ultimately failed to provide concrete evidence. The denial of the petition by the NTSB means that, for now, the truth behind TWA Flight 800 will remain shrouded in mystery.

The pervasive musty odor is likely a result of cellulose decay, a common issue in paper materials due to the presence of lignin, an unstable compound introduced in papermaking processes since the mid-19th century. This compound breaks down into acids, leading to the brittleness of paper. To combat this degradation, the Library of Congress has annually treated over 250,000 books with magnesium oxide since 2001. In a pioneering effort, chemist Lorraine Gibson of the University of Strathclyde in Scotland leads the Heritage Smells project, utilizing a handheld mass spectrometer to detect decay in its nascent stages by pinpointing the molecules responsible for the musty scent. By identifying and understanding the molecules accelerating decay, researchers can develop strategies to impede its progression. This article was originally featured in the January 2012 edition of Popular Science magazine.

Non-league Woking delivered a stunning upset as they triumphed 3-0 over League One side Bury at Gigg Lane to advance to the FA Cup second round. The National League team took the lead with a 30th-minute goal by Regan Charles-Cook, leaving Bury struggling to mount a comeback. Inih Effiong and substitute Jamie Philpot sealed the victory with late goals, leaving Bury's caretaker boss and his team stunned. The match was full of close calls and near misses, with both teams fighting hard for the win. Woking's impressive performance has set the stage for an exciting home tie in the next round. This thrilling display of skill and determination is a testament to the magic of the FA Cup, and Woking's triumph will be remembered as a shining moment in the competition's history.

In a dance of words and ideas, Adrian Goldberg unravels the intricate tapestry of the United States SOPA Bill, unveiling its new measures of enforcement with a solemn grace. As the melody of his voice weaves through the airwaves, he draws a comparison to the anti-piracy measures already entrenched in the UK, casting a shadow of uncertainty over the digital landscape. Standing at the crossroads of innovation and regulation, Alexis Ohanian, the visionary co-founder of Reddit, emerges as a beacon of resistance, leading the charge against SOPA's suffocating grasp. In a symphony of dissent, he raises his voice alongside the silenced giants of the internet, painting a portrait of protest with each pixelated stroke. On the opposing side of the spectrum, Christopher Marcich, the steadfast guardian of the Motion Picture Association, Europe, defends SOPA with fervor, championing its cause as a shield against the tide of digital piracy. But in the midst of this clash of titans, a truth emerges like a whisper in the wind – SOPA threatens to stifle the very essence of creativity and innovation, casting a shadow over the future of technology and art. As the echoes of this debate reverberate through the digital realm, the question lingers like a haunting refrain – will the melody of progress be silenced by the discord of regulation?

Inbox Cube isn't just another email client for iPhone - it's a game-changer. It's like a breath of fresh air in the world of mundane, text-based email interfaces. When you open the app, you're greeted with a visually stunning display of your attachments and files, making it easy to find what you need at a glance. The classic email view is there, but it's the unique features that really set Inbox Cube apart. The attachments tab showcases all your files in a visually appealing way, allowing you to easily sort and filter through them. As someone who tends to hold onto emails like precious treasures, I found the initial loading time for attachments a bit long, but it's well worth the wait. And the contacts tab is a stroke of genius, highlighting the people you interact with most frequently. Inbox Cube has truly revolutionized the way I manage my emails, and I can't imagine going back to the old way of doing things.

It would not be a complete Oakland Raiders game without a disappointing defeat and a physical altercation. During the recent match against the Cincinnati Bengals, tensions escalated between players when Bengals tackle Andrew Whitworth took issue with Raiders player Lamar Houston for aggressively tackling quarterback Andy Dalton. This incident led to a scuffle, with Tommy Kelly also becoming involved in the confrontation. The altercation, which resulted in all three players being ejected from the game, resembled more of a scuffle than a professional sports altercation. It is likely that the players involved will face further disciplinary action from the league, possibly in the form of fines. The Raiders, on the other hand, must find a way to channel their competitive spirit in a more constructive manner following their fourth consecutive loss.

Utilizing citronella candles outdoors is a practical method for mosquito control, but their potent scent may not be suitable for indoor use, particularly for individuals with respiratory issues. Avoiding the use of chemical-laden mosquito repellents inside the home is also recommended. For a natural alternative, consider using an oil burner with a carrier oil, such as almond or jojoba, combined with essential oils like peppermint, eucalyptus, and lemon eucalyptus. Another option is to burn lavender oil near entry points to deter mosquitoes from entering or lingering indoors. Additionally, placing bowls or saucers with citrus-scented dish soap in areas where mosquitoes are present, such as the kitchen, bathroom, or screened porch, can effectively control their presence indoors.

The idea of a physical PayPal store may initially appear unconventional, but it represents a strategic move by the company to showcase its latest in-store technologies. The upcoming pop-up store in Manhattan, set to open on November 1st, is a part of PayPal's promotional campaign aimed at highlighting its new mobile payment services. The location at 174 Hudson Street in Tribeca will feature a prominent QR code on its exterior, allowing passers-by to easily access more information on PayPal's offerings. Inside, merchants will have the opportunity to explore and engage with PayPal's various commercial services, such as location-based promotions, cross-device payment options, and real-time inventory tracking. The store's limited operation period of approximately three and a half months indicates a sense of urgency in introducing these new features to physical retailers. While specific partnerships have yet to be disclosed, it is anticipated that PayPal will soon announce collaborations with key industry players. This venture exemplifies PayPal's innovative approach to bridging the gap between online and offline commerce, ultimately enhancing the overall shopping experience for both consumers and businesses.

In a dance of fate and sorrow, Marouane Fellaini's warrior spirit was tested as he was forced to bow out early, his knee whispering secrets of pain. A symphony of fear played in Roberto Martinez's mind, as thoughts of ligament damage clouded the horizon. Yet, amidst the shadows, Yannick Carrasco's goal shone like a beacon of hope, sealing Belgium's triumph in a World Cup-bound journey.

In the heart of the battlefield, Belgium emerged victorious, their path to glory paved with the sweat and tears of a hard-fought battle. Thomas Meunier's opening verse painted a picture of dominance, only to be met with the defiant melody of Haris Medunjanin and Edin Visca. A tale of resilience unfolded as Michy Batshuayi and Jan Vertonghen reclaimed the lead, only to have it challenged by Dario Dumic's equalizer.

But in a twist of fate, Carrasco emerged as the hero of the day, his goal a crescendo of triumph in a symphony of perseverance. As Greece awaited their chance in the shadows, Belgium stood tall, their victory a testament to the unwavering spirit that fuels the beautiful game. And in the echoes of that fateful night, the melody of hope lingered, a reminder that even in the darkest hour, light will always find its way.

With the arrival of European settlers, the Indigenous people of Australia were forcibly stripped of their rich and vibrant culture, leaving deep scars that continue to manifest in mental health issues, high rates of suicide, and widespread alcohol abuse. In the Northern Territory, the grim reality is starkly evident as First Australians make up a staggering 86 percent of the prison population. Shockingly, many find themselves incarcerated for minor infractions such as unpaid fines, missed court dates, or minor traffic violations. In Darwin, a significant portion of this marginalized group are known as Long Grassers; a transient population predominantly comprised of Indigenous individuals who have been displaced from their remote communities and are ensnared in a vicious cycle of homelessness, addiction, and imprisonment. Amidst this harrowing backdrop, the traditional owners of Darwin, the Larrakia Nation, have steadfastly endeavored to combat these pressing issues through a myriad of social services, including the invaluable Night Patrols. We embarked on a poignant journey alongside these dedicated individuals to witness firsthand their tireless efforts to guide people back home, provide aid to the homeless, and ultimately break the cycle that leads Aboriginal people into the unforgiving clutches of the justice system. This poignant and revealing documentary serves as the second installment of our compelling series, Over Represented, delving deep into the profound issue of Indigenous incarceration. For more profound insights, be sure to watch Briggs - Live at Juvie and Barred Calls, and explore The Incarceration Issue, an enlightening special edition from the esteemed VICE.

In a heartening display of compassion and concern, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has taken a proactive stance towards assisting the most vulnerable members of society during the harsh winter conditions prevailing in the state. It is evident that his directive to district magistrates to prioritize the well-being of the poor, destitute, and homeless individuals reflects a genuine commitment to alleviating their suffering. The Chief Minister's stern warning against any negligence in providing relief underscores the importance of a consistent and diligent approach in addressing the needs of those in dire circumstances. The swift implementation of relief measures, including the establishment of night shelters, lighting of bonfires, and distribution of free blankets, is a testament to the government's dedication to ensuring the welfare of its citizens. As the number of bonfires lit, blankets distributed, and night shelters set up continues to rise, it is reassuring to see the tangible impact of these efforts in providing warmth and comfort to those in need.

When considering watering practices for your garden, landscape, or restoration project, it is essential to take into account the specific conditions of your location. If the search results suggest a watering schedule that is either too harsh or too lenient, it is advisable to select a nearby zipcode that better represents the characteristics of your area. After the initial year of planting, it is crucial to adjust your watering frequency and duration based on the changing seasons. In Spring, for example, you may need to water more frequently to support new growth, while in Summer, you may need longer watering sessions to combat the heat. Fall and Winter will require different watering schedules to accommodate the changing climate conditions. By experimenting with different watering seasons, frequencies, and durations, you can optimize the health and growth of your plants, taking into account factors such as sun exposure, soil type, and ecological impact. It is important to note that these adjustments may significantly influence the outcome of your garden or landscape, so it is crucial to monitor and adapt your watering practices accordingly.

Prepare to be enchanted by a special treat that has been long-awaited by many - a My Little Mages rendition of Sombra. Initially hesitant to tackle the task due to the belief that there was little room for innovation in portraying the enigmatic character, a spark of inspiration led to a unique approach that promises to captivate the imagination. In this fantastical universe, Sombra's essence as a smoke monster is seamlessly fused with a solid human form, manifested as a suit of armor. While the intricate details of medieval armor may have initially deterred the artist, the challenge of achieving symmetry and depth only serves to enhance the allure of this mystical creation. Prepare to be enthralled as the enigmatic Sombra takes on a new, captivating form in this imaginative interpretation.

Hey there, gamers! Want to stay in the loop with all the latest news and videos for your favorite game? Well, get ready for some exciting updates on the Metal Gear Solid movie! This "hot British writer" is no stranger to the big screen, having worked on films like Monsters: Dark Continent and Fast Girls. And while we're still in the dark about the plot and casting choices, one thing's for sure - this film is shaping up to be one epic adventure. And don't forget to mark your calendars for the release of Metal Gear Solid: The Phantom Pain - it's going to be a wild ride!

Officials at Ursinus College confirmed that a norovirus outbreak was responsible for the widespread stomach illness that afflicted over 200 students last week. This alarming revelation highlights a serious lapse in hygiene and sanitation protocols at the college. The fact that classes had to be canceled, events were disrupted, and students had to seek medical treatment due to this preventable virus is simply unacceptable. It is clear that urgent measures need to be implemented to ensure the safety and well-being of the student body. The reopening of the dining hall after a mere inspection is a cause for concern, as it suggests a lack of thoroughness in addressing the issue. The college's promise of "aggressive cleaning, sanitizing, and disinfecting efforts" rings hollow in the face of this outbreak. It is imperative that a more rigorous and comprehensive approach be taken to prevent such incidents from recurring in the future.

From the streets of Ontario to the sunny fields of Orlando, Cyle Larin and Richie Laryea are living out a childhood dream together. These two best friends have been inseparable since they were just nine years old, playing side by side for their youth club Sigma FC. They may have taken different paths for college, with Larin heading to UConn and Laryea to Akron, but fate brought them back together when Larin was drafted by Orlando City as the first overall pick in 2015. Larin's record-breaking rookie season set the stage for Laryea to join him in Orlando, as the seventh overall pick in the SuperDraft. Now, as roommates in their shared apartment outside Orlando, they are each other's biggest supporters and motivators as they strive for success on the field. The latest episode of MLS Insider presented by adidas, "Cyle and Richie", gives a behind-the-scenes look at the journey of these two talented Canadians as they chase their dreams in the MLS.

The milestone of Mathew Stokes' 200th and final game for Essendon has been announced by Coach John Worsfold, which will take place on Sunday as the Bombers face the Western Bulldogs at Etihad Stadium. This news was confirmed on the club's website with minimal fanfare, coinciding with the celebration of Adam Cooney's 250th game. Stokes, aged 31, was persuaded to return for one last season as a top-up player, following the year-long doping bans imposed on 12 Bombers. After being delisted by Geelong at the conclusion of the previous season, the two-time premiership player opted to join Essendon alongside longtime teammate James Kelly. Despite being limited by hamstring and groin injuries, Stokes participated in 10 matches this season, averaging 18 disposals per game. With 209 goals from 199 games, he was a pivotal member of the Cats' 2007 and '11 premiership sides.

The bustling city of Miami serves as the backdrop for this political and business intrigue. The sun beats down on the vibrant streets, casting a golden glow over the palm trees swaying in the warm breeze. The scent of Cuban coffee and fresh seafood wafts through the air, mingling with the sounds of salsa music and chatter in multiple languages. As Jeffrey Loria, the owner of the Miami Marlins, navigates the city's busy streets, the colorful Art Deco architecture of South Beach provides a stunning contrast to the sleek skyscrapers of downtown. In the midst of this lively scene, the White House chief of staff, Reince Priebus, strategizes in a sleek office overlooking the glittering waters of Biscayne Bay. The possibility of Loria serving as the ambassador to France adds an air of excitement and uncertainty to the already dynamic atmosphere of Miami.

Once upon a time, five individuals embarked on a reckless endeavor that inadvertently unleashed chaos upon the 21st Century. Now faced with the repercussions of their actions, they must confront the looming threat of societal decay in an effort to safeguard humanity's existence. INJECTION, a groundbreaking ongoing series developed by the esteemed creative team behind Moon Knight, seamlessly blends elements of science fiction, horror, crime fiction, techno-thriller, and ghostly encounters. Through a serialized format, the graphic novels explore the escalating peculiarity of our world, juxtaposing a tumultuous future with a haunting past that converge upon the present. Follow the journey of five unconventional visionaries as they navigate the paranormal and metaphysical realms, grappling with the consequences of their creation, the Injection, which has left an indelible mark on the planet.

In the hustle and bustle of the city's heart,
A grandmother and her granddaughters did depart.
With bags in hand and little ones in tow,
They rushed to catch the train before it could go.

But fate had a cruel twist in store,
As the doors closed, leaving her on the platform floor.
In a mere 10 seconds, her world torn asunder,
Her heart heavy with fear and thunder.

Metro's regret echoed through the station,
As the children were carried away without hesitation.
A grandmother left behind, her arms empty and cold,
While her granddaughters were swept away, their fate untold.

In the blink of an eye, the train was gone,
Leaving a grandmother to grieve and mourn.
But in the chaos and despair,
A glimmer of hope, a helping hand was there.

Through the tears and the pain,
Metro staff reunited the family again.
But the scars of that day will forever remain,
A grandmother's heart forever stained.

In the rhythm of the city's beat,
A tale of loss and reunion, bittersweet.
May Metro learn from this mistake,
And never again a family's heartbreak.

In the rugged terrain of north eastern Afghanistan, a senior al-Qaeda leader met his demise at the hands of a US drone strike, according to US military officials. Farouq al-Qahtani, the organization's formidable leader in the region, is believed to have been extinguished on a somber Sunday, sources whispered in the shadows. Reports from NBC news suggest that his second-in-command also faced the wrath of a separate strike. The strikes, shrouded in secrecy, took place in the mysterious province of Kunar, their true impact yet to be unveiled to the world. Al-Qahtani, a Saudi-born Qatari national, found himself on the infamous US list of most wanted terrorists in the chilly month of February. His alleged involvement in diabolical schemes targeting Europe and the United States had painted a target on his back. Afghan government spokesman Abdul Ghani Mosamem revealed that a total of 15 insurgents, including two Arabs and a band of Pakistani Taliban fighters, met their end in the relentless operation on that fateful Sunday.

Keisuke Honda, the talented Japanese midfielder, stands resolute in his determination to secure his place at the prestigious AC Milan, undeterred by the looming arrival of Kevin-Prince Boateng. Despite the swirling rumors of a potential move away from the club, the 29-year-old maestro remains steadfast in his commitment to vie for his spot alongside the enigmatic former Schalke outcast. As whispers of Boateng's potential departure for England flutter through the air, with both West Ham and Everton expressing interest, Honda has adamantly affirmed his allegiance to the Rossoneri, poised to wage a fierce battle against the Ghanaian international for his rightful place. With Boateng on the cusp of sealing a permanent deal with AC Milan in the upcoming January, following a spellbinding trial, it was widely assumed that Honda's tenure was nearing its end. Yet, the resolute midfielder has gallantly declared his intention to stay and fight for a prominent role within the esteemed Milan ranks.

Hey everyone, have you heard the latest recruiting drama in college football? Three-star Miami cornerback Sheldrick Redwine just pulled a last-minute switcheroo and withdrew his commitment to Louisville! Can you believe it? The Cardinals were trying to lock down his shaky commitment, but it looks like he's keeping his options open. He just visited the University of Texas and now Auburn is in the mix too. Will Louisville snag another talented cornerback like Javarius Davis or will Auburn swoop in and steal the spotlight once again? And let's not forget about Jacksonville speedster Jalen Julius and junior-college standout Treston Decoud - the recruiting game is heating up, folks! Stay tuned for the next chapter in this wild ride of college football recruiting.

Have you heard about the 120W ACI Off-Road LED Light Bar? It's got a bunch of powerful LEDs that really light up the road, way better than just your regular headlights. This bad boy has a combo beam pattern and packs a whopping 10,800 lumens in a slim package. The center LEDs give you a super focused 8-degree spot beam with 9,000 lumens, while the ones on the ends spread out a nice 90-degree flood pattern with an extra 1,800 lumens. A resident of the Valley has been accused of assaulting his parents both inside and outside of their residence in Chandler. According to the Chandler Police Department, on October 27, 28-year-old James Anthony McPherson entered the kitchen unclothed and proceeded to sit at the table. Subsequently, his mother exited the room and heard the sounds of a dispute and property being damaged. Law enforcement officials assert that the altercation escalated to physical violence when McPherson pursued his father into the bedroom. Although his mother attempted to leave the premises, she was intercepted in the garage and forcibly brought back into the home. McPherson positioned himself in the doorway, preventing their departure. According to police reports, McPherson knocked his father to the ground and forcefully struck his head against the kitchen floor. His mother was ultimately able to flee and seek refuge at a neighbor's residence, but was intercepted before she could alert them. McPherson forcibly returned his mother to the home, pushed her to the floor, and restrained her there. Police reports further indicate that McPherson proceeded to assault his father using a Swiffer Wet Jet, inflicting injury to his eye and causing him to bleed. On her third attempt to escape, his mother sought assistance from neighbors, who were able to extricate her husband from the residence and transport him to a medical facility. McPherson was apprehended the following day and reportedly informed law enforcement that he recollected the altercation but not the specifics, attributing his lack of clarity to alcohol consumption. Police discovered an empty bottle of whiskey in his room and within the residence.

For generations, the citizens of Chicago have reveled in the exquisite public spaces that grace the city's park district. Thankfully, the Library of Congress has meticulously documented decades of images capturing Windy City residents basking in the splendor of the great outdoors. Chicagoans hold a deep-seated pride in their cherished public spaces, eagerly anticipating the unveiling of new parks currently in development. Among these treasured sites, Grant Park stands as a shining beacon at the heart of the city, boasting iconic tourist attractions. Just a stone's throw away lies the illustrious Lincoln Park, a sprawling oasis steeped in history and grandeur. Venturing further north, one encounters Edgewater Beach, once a playground for the elite and affluent. Take a leisurely stroll through time and immerse yourself in the rich tapestry of Chicago's past through these captivating images capturing the essence of the city's magnificent public spaces.

Many individuals familiar with summer camps or popular culture are likely to have encountered the well-known prank of submerging a sleeping person's hand in water to induce urination. This prank is based on the belief that the sensation of water can trigger the sleeper's bladder, leading to involuntary urination. While numerous anecdotal accounts support this belief, MythBusters Jamie Hyneman and Adam Savage sought to investigate its validity. To do so, they conducted an experiment in which they and crew member Matt took turns being monitored while sleeping. Despite their efforts, the prank did not yield the expected results, as no incidents of involuntary urination occurred. Therefore, the MythBusters concluded that the hand-in-water prank was not effective in inducing urination while asleep.

The crash of the FlyDubai Boeing 737 in Russia's Rostov-on-Don has raised questions about the actions of the aircraft's commander. According to reports from PravdaRu and Interfax news agency, the commander may have deliberately sent the plane into a nosedive, as indicated by the flight recorder data. The commander's response to the co-pilot's questions and the alleged conflict between the pilots prior to the crash have also come under scrutiny. However, the Interstate Aviation Committee has stated that they do not have enough information to confirm whether the commander's actions were voluntary. The crash, which occurred during the aircraft's second landing attempt, resulted in the tragic loss of 55 passengers and seven crew members. These findings highlight the complexity of the investigation and the need for a thorough examination of all factors leading up to the crash.

It is with heavy hearts and tear-stained eyes that we must convey the devastating news of Jana Robeyst's untimely passing on April 8th, 2016. Her vibrant spirit, unwavering dedication, and profound love for the wild forest elephants at Mbeli Bai, Nouabale-Ndoki National Park, have left a void that can never be filled. Jana was not just a scientist; she was a force of nature, a beacon of light in the dense African rainforest she called home. Her passion for the majestic creatures she studied was palpable, her joy infectious as she spent her days immersed in the sights and sounds of the bai. From the moment she set foot in Congo in December 2013, Jana's presence at the Mbeli Bai Study was nothing short of transformative. Her commitment to the cause was unwavering, her impact immeasurable. Even in her final days, Jana's dedication to sharing her knowledge and nurturing the next generation of researchers remained steadfast. The loss of Jana Robeyst is not just a loss for the scientific community, but for all who were touched by her grace, kindness, and unwavering love for the natural world. She may be gone, but her legacy will forever live on in the hearts of those who were fortunate enough to know her.

Dez Bryant's desire to remain a Dallas Cowboy for the long haul is no secret. According to NFL Media columnist Michael Silver, Bryant is eager to secure a long-term contract with the team in the upcoming offseason, as revealed by his advisor David Wells. Despite currently playing on his rookie contract set to expire at the end of the 2015 season, Bryant's dedication and passion for the Cowboys is undeniable.

During a recent game against the Detroit Lions, Bryant's emotions got the best of him as he passionately urged his team on, including a spirited exchange with quarterback Tony Romo. However, footage of the incident showed Bryant's intensity and fervor rather than anger, a display that only solidified the Cowboys' commitment to him, as reported by NFL Media Insider Ian Rapoport. Cowboys COO Stephen Jones expressed unwavering support for Bryant, emphasizing the team's love for him.

The heated sideline moment also involved discussions with veteran players Jason Witten and DeMarcus Ware, with Bryant acknowledging his animated behavior. Despite some colorful language used, both Ware and Witten were focused on guiding Bryant's attention back to the game at hand, emphasizing the need for unity and concentration in crucial moments. Ultimately, Bryant's passion for the game and determination to succeed shine through, making him an integral part of the Cowboys' future plans.

The president of Turkey has declared that all individuals suspected of plotting a coup or involved in terrorist activities will be required to wear a specific almond-brown uniform when appearing in court. Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced that those accused of participating in the July 2016 coup plot will be mandated to wear jumpsuits, while individuals associated with Fethullah Gulen and Kurdish rebels will be required to wear jackets and trousers. This measure comes in response to a defendant appearing in court wearing a "Hero" T-shirt, leading to the subsequent detainment of nearly 30 individuals for similar attire. President Erdogan emphasized the necessity of imposing a uniform dress code in court, citing the need to prevent defendants from wearing inappropriate attire. Additionally, he expressed the desire for a prisoner uniform similar to those worn in Guantanamo Bay, highlighting the government's determination to eradicate all individuals associated with the coup plot. This crackdown has resulted in the detainment of over 50,000 people and the suspension of 150,000 public servants, drawing significant international criticism for its sweeping nature and the imposition of a state of emergency.

Hey guys, guess what? The ACT Brumbies are stepping up their game by launching their very own TV show next week! They're the first Super Rugby team to do it, and they're teaming up with Network Ten to bring it to you on One HD. The show, hosted by Stephanie Brantz, is set to kick off and give fans a behind-the-scenes look at all things Brumbies. And it couldn't come at a better time as the club is working hard to boost their membership drive. With less than 7000 sign-ups so far, they're aiming to hit 11,000 by the end of the year. But CEO Michael Jones is staying positive and believes they can make it happen. So tune in and support your Brumbies as they take on the Hurricanes at Canberra Stadium!

The story of Ballou Jean-Yves Tabla is a tale of raw talent and relentless determination. Born in the Ivory Coast but raised in Canada, this young winger has captured the hearts of fans and scouts alike with his electrifying performances. At just 17 years old, Tabla has already been named Canadian Under-17 Player of the Year, a testament to his skill and potential. His journey from the streets of Montreal to the training grounds of Chelsea alongside legends like Didier Drogba is nothing short of inspirational. Tabla's recent victory over England's U20 team has only heightened the interest of Europe's top clubs, who are now vying for the chance to witness his brilliance up close. As the world watches and waits, one thing is certain: Ballou Jean-Yves Tabla is a star on the rise, destined for greatness.

The test flight of the US military's Falcon HTV-2, touted as the 'world's fastest plane', ended in failure as the vehicle crashed into the Pacific Ocean. The aircraft, which is capable of traveling 22 times faster than a commercial airliner, was launched from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California attached to a rocket. However, after approximately nine minutes, the craft ceased transmitting signals and is presumed to have descended into the ocean. Engineers had intended to guide the plane on a hypersonic flight, with expectations of reaching speeds of around 13,000mph upon its return to Earth. The aircraft, designed for research purposes, is capable of traveling at approximately 20 times the speed of sound and withstanding temperatures of 2,000C. A previous launch attempt was halted in April due to a fault on board the aircraft, and a second attempt on Wednesday was postponed to Thursday due to adverse weather conditions.

In Mangaluru, BJP MP Anant Kumar Hegde has come under scrutiny for his reported remarks that have been perceived as derogatory towards Islam and Muslims during a press conference in Sirsi, Uttara Kannada district. The Dakshina Kannada district unit of youth Congress has lodged a police complaint against the Uttara Kannada MP, accusing him of making blasphemous and insulting comments. In response to the complaint, Youth Congress district vice president Luqman Bantwal expressed concern over the alleged impact of Hegde's statements on the Muslim community. Additionally, Dakshina Kannada Kazi Twaka Ahmed Musliyar has called on the state government to address what he views as anti-Islam rhetoric from the MP. State Health Minister U T Khader has also urged Home Minister G Parameshwara to take action against Hegde for his controversial remarks.

San Diego Chargers quarterback Philip Rivers exhibited remarkable resilience during Saturday night's overtime victory against the San Francisco 49ers, as reported by team sources to ESPN. Despite facing a challenging circumstance, Rivers demonstrated unwavering determination while playing with a bulging disk in his lower back, a condition that medical professionals have expressed concerns may escalate into a herniation. This physical ailment prompted Rivers to forgo practice on Wednesday, marking the first time he has missed practice since 2007. The discomfort initially surfaced three weeks prior, prompting Rivers to seek relief through epidural injections to alleviate swelling. While he remains hopeful to avoid surgery during the offseason, the possibility remains on the table, as noted by sources. Despite these challenges, Rivers delivered an impressive performance during Saturday's game, completing 33 out of 54 passes for 356 yards. His four touchdown passes, in addition to crucial conversions on fourth-and-8 and fourth-and-10 during the final drive, were instrumental in the Chargers' comeback victory after trailing by 21 points at halftime, bolstering the team's playoff aspirations.

Fear not, for this truck is not a voracious consumer of electricity. In fact, it's the opposite - it actually generates more electricity than it uses. This isn't some magical perpetual motion machine, but rather a marvel of physics that harnesses regenerative braking as its main source of energy. As the e-Dumper ascends the mountain, it consumes around 30 kWh of energy. But on the way back down, carrying a massive 120,000 pounds of rock, it actually generates a surplus of 10 kWh thanks to regenerative braking. Throughout the day, the truck is expected to make 20 trips, not only dumping rocks but also returning as much as 200 kWh of extra energy back into the grid.

Komatsu has long been at the forefront of utilizing electric power in its trucks, having released hybrid diesel-electric powerplants as early as 2009. And now, this modified Komatsu dump truck, designed by heavy equipment manufacturer Kuhn Schweiz and Swiss battery storage company Lithium Storage, is a testament to the growing trend of businesses seeking alternative, more sustainable vehicle options. With the potential for governmental bans on fossil-fuel vehicles in the near future, the e-Dumper is a glimpse into the very real possibilities of the future of commercial vehicles.

The city's transportation initiatives, the citywide ferry service and the Brooklyn-Queens Connector streetcar, may be at odds with each other, according to a recent report. Both services will serve the same neighborhoods along the Brooklyn and Queens waterfront, leading experts to question their compatibility. The planned stops for both the ferry and the streetcar are nearly identical, raising concerns about potential competition between the two. However, supporters of both initiatives argue that they offer unique benefits. The ferry provides east to west service, while the streetcar will be essential as large-scale development continues in the area. Despite the potential conflict, the citywide ferry service is set to launch next summer, with the streetcar following in 2024 at the earliest.

Mayor Thomas Menino's impending announcement of his decision not to seek re-election is shrouded in secrecy and speculation. Sources indicate that the mayor's health may be a factor in his choice, with unnamed individuals suggesting that his doctors have warned him against the physical demands of a campaign. Despite Menino's recent return home from a period of health struggles, concerns about his stamina persist, with close associates hinting at his weakened state at the end of the work day. The mayor's inner circle, including spokesperson Dot Joyce, strategist Mike Kineavy, and best friend Mike Galvin, remains tight-lipped, leaving the public to speculate about the true reasons behind Menino's decision. This air of mystery is compounded by rumors of a future position at Boston University, adding further intrigue to the mayor's unexpected exit from the political stage. Menino's ascent to the mayoralty, following the resignation of Ray Flynn, has been historic, but his departure now raises questions about the circumstances surrounding his decision and the legacy he leaves behind.

Hey everyone, did you hear about the protest in Jakarta against the Miss World pageant happening in Bali this weekend? A group of over 200 Indonesian Muslim hard-liners gathered outside the MNC Tower, where the local organizer of the contest is located. They held up banners with messages like "Reject Miss World that exploits women" and "Go to hell Miss World" while chanting "Allah akbar" outside the building. The protest leader, Muhammad Al Khathath, called the pageant an insult and humiliation to women, urging Muslims to reject it. Despite the controversy, the demonstration remained peaceful and ended after a meeting with the pageant organizers. It's interesting to see the clash of cultures and values in this diverse country, as some contestants have already arrived for the competition. The Miss World Organization has agreed to make changes to the competition, including eliminating the bikini round and having contestants wear more conservative attire. It's a reminder that even in a country like Indonesia, with its majority moderate Muslim population, there are still voices of dissent and resistance to certain cultural practices.

Hey, did you hear about the thirty fugitives wanted for war crimes or crimes against humanity believed to be hiding in Canada? Yeah, Prime Minister Stephen Harper's government just revealed that info. The Border Services Agency website even named the suspects and is asking for the public's help in tracking them down. They're from all over - the Middle East, Africa, Latin America - you name it. Public Safety Minister Vic Toews is adamant that these suspects need to be found and removed from Canada. The website mentioned countries like Afghanistan, Algeria, Angola, and more. No specific charges were listed, but the Border Services Agency set up a hotline for anyone with tips. And get this - Immigration Minister Jason Kenney announced plans to revoke the citizenship of 1,800 people suspected of fraudulently obtaining their status. Crazy stuff, right?

The US Senate recently approved a bill aimed at funding government operations from October 1 to November 15 in order to prevent agency shutdowns. Notably, no Republicans voted in favor of the emergency funding measure that was passed on Friday. Senate Majority Leader Harry Reid, a Democrat, emphasized the importance of passing the bill as a way to convey a message to what he referred to as "radical Republicans" who have been obstructing government operations by attempting to dismantle the US healthcare law, commonly known as 'Obamacare'. Additionally, various business groups, including the US Chamber of Commerce, have urged Congress to swiftly pass the spending bill and raise the government's borrowing limit. The 79-19 vote to end debate on the Senate bill represented a setback for Republican Senator Ted Cruz, who had been attempting to delay the process by insisting that government funds should only be approved if President Barack Obama's healthcare law was halted. Notably, fewer than half of Cruz's fellow Republicans supported his stance. The bill is expected to face challenges in the House, where many Republicans are pushing to include an 'Obamacare amendment' or other provisions that Democrats would likely view as unacceptable. Should the House proceed with such measures, it could lead to a deadlock and potentially result in a government shutdown on Tuesday, potentially affecting up to 800,000 federal employees through furloughs.

A lawsuit alleging sexual harassment has been filed against pop star Britney Spears by her former bodyguard, Fernando Flores. In the legal complaint, Mr. Flores claims that Ms. Spears engaged in inappropriate behavior, such as repeatedly exposing herself and engaging in sexual activities in his presence. Additionally, he alleges that the singer's tumultuous relationship with her boyfriend resulted in emotional distress, particularly when their arguments occurred in front of her children. While Ms. Spears' legal representation chose not to comment on the matter, a lawyer representing her ex-husband, Kevin Federline, dismissed the accusations as unfounded. According to court documents filed in Los Angeles Superior Court, Mr. Flores asserts that he was subjected to unwanted advances and witnessed concerning behavior towards the singer's children. However, Mr. Kaplan, representing Mr. Federline, has stated that the claims were thoroughly investigated prior to the lawsuit being initiated and found to lack credibility. He emphasized that any allegations of misconduct or harm towards the children are taken seriously and that the motivations behind the accusations appear to be financially driven. Mr. Flores, who worked for Ms. Spears from February to July of the current year, also implicates his security firm employers for disregarding or belittling his grievances regarding the singer's alleged conduct.

North Korea's armed forces minister issued a chilling warning on Thursday, declaring the country's readiness to wage a "holy war" against South Korea, even threatening to utilize its nuclear arsenal. This provocation came as South Korea displayed a robust show of strength in an effort to deter further aggression from its unpredictable neighbor. Kim Yong Chun, North Korea's defense chief, brazenly proclaimed at a patriotic rally honoring the military accomplishments of Kim Jong-il, that Pyongyang stood prepared to launch a "sacred war" should the South infringe upon its territory. South Korea responded by conducting its largest military exercise of the year, a month after a deadly North Korean artillery attack that claimed four lives on a South Korean island. The show of force, conducted just 30 miles south of the heavily fortified border, consisted of 800 troops, tanks, aircraft, artillery, rockets, and gunships, underscoring the escalating tensions on the peninsula.

Environmental regulators are currently investigating yet another overflow from a dam at the Bengalla coal mine, marking the third recent mine spill in the Hunter region that is under review. Despite assertions from mine operators, Rio Tinto, that there was no dam wall failure, the spillage began last Friday. This incident follows the collapse of walls at two other sites in the region - Rio's Warkworth mine and Peabody Energy's Wambo mine - during heavy rains earlier this month, potentially resulting in the discharge of millions of litres of sediment-laden water into nearby rivers. The NSW Environment Protection Authority reported that water from the dam was still flowing from the Warkworth mine site as of Friday, although a Rio spokesman claimed that the release had ceased by that time. The frequency of these spills raises concerns about the environmental impact and the effectiveness of current safety measures at these mining sites.

The Seattle Seahawks released Drew Nowak last week, despite him being their starting center at the beginning of the previous season. Nowak was quickly picked up by the Kansas City Chiefs, who also signed three players that stood out during the rookie minicamp tryouts. The Chiefs added offensive linemen Zach Sterup and Garrick Mayweather, as well as defensive back Shannon Edwards to their roster. In order to accommodate these new signings, the Chiefs released offensive linemen Jake Bernstein, Ben Clarke, and Laurence Gibson, along with defensive back Jordan Kovacs. Nowak had lost his starting position midway through the previous season and spent the remainder of the year on the practice squad. He was re-signed by the Seahawks during the offseason, but was ultimately released to make room for incoming undrafted rookies.

The Massachusetts State Police (MSP) has taken steps to address the officer's actions by placing him on restricted duty. Despite efforts to reach out to Kin Moy, the individual who recorded the video depicting the trooper's use of pepper spray during a demonstration in Boston, he has not been responsive. In a statement, the MSP expressed their frustration with Moy's lack of cooperation, stating that he has not responded to multiple requests for contact. Moy, on the other hand, has indicated that he is seeking counsel from the ACLU and an attorney before engaging further with the official investigation. This delay in cooperation raises questions about transparency and accountability in the handling of this incident.

The enigmatic demise of six-year-old JonBenet Ramsey stands as one of the most captivating murder cases in recent memory, a haunting enigma that continues to captivate the nation. Even years after the tragic event, the mystery remains shrouded in darkness, refusing to yield its secrets. Who was responsible for the untimely demise of the young beauty queen, and for what nefarious reason? Who sought to conceal the truth, and who wove a web of deceit? In "JonBenet", a definitive and masterful exploration of the Ramsey murder, esteemed former lead Boulder Police detective Steve Thomas delves deep into the shadows, unraveling the case with mesmerizing precision and attention to detail. With a keen eye for the tantalizing nuances that others dare not contemplate, Thomas raises a host of compelling questions that pierce the veil of the investigation's mishandling. How did the authorities fumble the initial stages of the inquiry, allowing the crime scene to be desecrated with reckless abandon? Why were John and Patsy Ramsey shielded from early scrutiny and polygraph tests, despite their erratic and suspicious behavior? What vital evidence was overlooked, and which crucial witnesses were left unquestioned? And why were the Ramseys privy to confidential information about the case, even gaining access to sensitive police reports? These and many other inquiries form the cornerstone of Thomas's piercing analysis, shedding light on a saga that remains as beguiling as it is perplexing.

The Indian government has approved the prosecution of 21 internet firms, including Facebook, Yahoo! and Google, in response to allegations of posting obscene content online. This authorization may result in company directors being summoned to a trial court in New Delhi to address serious charges such as inciting religious hatred and promoting social discord, according to sources. The case, initially brought forth by local journalist Vinay Rai, accused the websites of hosting offensive material and violating laws aimed at preserving religious harmony and national unity in India. An example cited in the case is a controversial online cartoon of Savita Bhabhi, which sparked outrage and was ultimately censored by the Indian government.

Trade Commissioner Karel de Gucht issued a stern warning to Russia, emphasizing that any actions taken against one member state of the European Union will be considered as an affront to the entire EU. This warning came during a discussion on heightened customs inspections at the Russia-Lithuania border, where Russian officials have been subjecting Lithuanian trucks to lengthy and burdensome checks, causing significant delays and queues. In response, Lithuanian Foreign Minister Linas Linkevicius raised the possibility of retaliatory measures at the border with Kaliningrad, a Russian territory surrounded by Lithuania and Poland and an important port on the Baltic Sea. During an urgent debate with Members of the European Parliament on 8 October 2013, Mr de Gucht mentioned the potential summoning of the Russian ambassador and acknowledged the complexity of the situation, stating that he was compiling a comprehensive list of issues faced in dealings with Russia. These increased checks have raised suspicions of a retaliatory motive following the European Commission's investigation into alleged market manipulation by Russia's Gazprom. For more information, please refer to the European Parliament's guidelines on the use of simultaneous interpretations and Democracy Live's overview of the plenary sessions.

A multitude of Palestinian demonstrators convened along Gaza's borders with Israel last Friday, amidst dire warnings from international human rights organizations regarding the imminent collapse of essential services in the region due to a deepening electricity crisis. The Gaza Strip is currently grappling with a severe shortage of electricity, leaving its populace of two million inhabitants with a mere fraction of power each day. This critical situation has upended numerous facets of daily life in the Hamas-controlled enclave, sparking concerns of an impending humanitarian catastrophe. Recent actions taken by Israel to curtail electricity provision to Gaza to a mere three hours daily, following a reduction in funding by Palestinian Authority President Mahmoud Abbas, have further exacerbated the situation. This move, widely interpreted as a tactic to exert pressure on the rival Hamas faction, has drawn condemnation from the UN humanitarian coordinator for the occupied Palestinian territories, Robert Piper, who has forewarned of dire consequences. The resultant power outages, compounded by surging demand during the month of Ramadan, have led to erratic blackouts lasting only two to four hours at a stretch, necessitating meticulous planning by residents for essential tasks such as refrigeration, healthcare, and personal hygiene. With hospitals reliant on generators and scarce fuel supplies, and many households reliant on electric water pumps, the absence of electricity has left many without access to basic necessities.

A mere centimeter in length and dating back approximately 240 million years, a fossilized bone serves as a testament to the ancestral lineage of colossal lizards still thriving in the lush landscapes of New Zealand, predating even the reign of dinosaurs. Unearthed not in the verdant lands of New Zealand, but in the ancient soils of Vellberg, Germany, this jaw bone sheds light on the history of the tuatara, pushing its origins back by a staggering 10 to 15 million years. Rainer Schoch, esteemed curator at the Stuttgart Natural History Museum, expressed in the esteemed pages of BMC Evolutionary Biology that this discovery, alongside subsequent findings such as a complete skeletal structure, promises to enrich our understanding of the evolution of these enigmatic reptiles, bearing familial ties to both serpents and monitor lizards. Measuring a modest five to ten centimeters, this species is distinguished by the peculiar trait of teeth protruding directly from the jaw. "Our early specimen is a veritable treasure trove of tuatara anatomy," Schoch remarked. Revered as "living fossils," tuatara persist on secluded isles dotting the New Zealand coastline, embodying an enduring lineage that has stood the test of time. While Schoch hesitates to embrace the term 'living fossil,' the remarkable longevity and steadfastness of this lineage cannot be denied. The dig site in south-western Germany has yielded a plethora of new species over the past thirteen years, with hopes high for further discoveries among the ancient rocks. Noteworthy findings in Vellberg reach lengths of up to six meters, captivating the attention of esteemed paleontologists from Washington, Buenos Aires, London, and Berlin.

The tragic deaths of a 23-year-old woman and a 28-year-old man in Mullah Quli village, Kunduz province, were reported by Mohammad Ayob, the governor of Imam Sahib district. The couple was stoned to death by Taliban insurgents, following a public confession of their extramarital affair. The man was identified as being married to another woman, while the woman was engaged to someone else. The brutal punishment, carried out in front of approximately 100 people, including Taliban fighters, involved the couple being bound and forced to stand in an empty field as stones were thrown at them until they succumbed to their injuries. This incident reflects the Taliban's strict adherence to Islamic Sharia law, which prescribes death by stoning for individuals found guilty of engaging in extramarital relationships. The gruesome execution of the couple serves as a chilling reminder of the Taliban's oppressive rule between 1996 and 2001, characterized by severe punishments for perceived transgressions, such as amputations for theft and public executions for alleged spies. The recent resurgence of such brutal practices in regions under Taliban control underscores the continued threat posed by the militant group as the conflict in Afghanistan enters its ninth year.

The folks at Project Aura, Google's wearable tech division, have been pulling out all the stops to bring us the next generation of Glass headsets. And let me tell you, they've been cooking up some seriously cool stuff. In the latest FCC filings, we caught a sneak peek at a workplace-friendly version of Glass that can actually be folded and tucked into your pocket like a regular old pair of specs. Plus, it's got some serious upgrades under the hood, including faster Wi-Fi, a better battery, and a beefed-up camera. And get this, the prism display is getting a major boost, offering a wider field of view. And to top it all off, it's built to be waterproof and super durable, perfect for those rough and tumble work environments. While Google hasn't spilled all the beans on a release date or price, they've already handed out hundreds of units to partners in their Glass for Work program. So, it looks like we might be seeing this bad boy in action sooner rather than later. Exciting stuff, right? Who knows, maybe we'll all be rocking our own pair of high-tech Google Glasses in the not-so-distant future.

An Oregon woman, Shellie Hubbard, found herself engulfed in a tumultuous argument with her boyfriend, Darwin Vonschirmer, last December as they traveled down a Washington State highway. The tension between them was palpable as they navigated the winding roads, their relationship teetering on the brink of collapse. In a fit of rage, Hubbard lashed out, slicing Vonschirmer's hand with a jagged piece of a broken coffee mug. But the true horror unfolded when she callously hurled their beloved Catahoula leopard hound dog, Peanut Butter, out of the car and into the path of oncoming traffic. The heart-wrenching thud as Peanut Butter met his untimely end reverberated through the air, a tragic consequence of Hubbard's unfathomable actions.

As the dust settled on the horrific scene, Hubbard's fate was sealed as she pleaded guilty to a litany of charges including first-degree animal cruelty, third-degree assault, and possession of methamphetamine. The individual in question was employed by a company specializing in the production of helicopter parts, primarily for the German military. The individual contended that his religious beliefs should remain a private matter, emphasizing that his membership in the organization was not indicative of any potential security risk. However, the court ruling on Tuesday upheld the decision to withhold security clearance, citing concerns surrounding the practice of auditing within Scientology, which involves the documentation of personal thoughts and experiences. This, the court argued, raises legitimate doubts regarding the trustworthiness of individuals associated with Scientology and their allegiance to the state constitution. Furthermore, the court emphasized that the denial of security clearance did not infringe upon the individual's freedom of religion. Tragically, two individuals with asthma succumbed to the cold. Mr. Room highlighted the urgent need for blankets and warm clothing for the 1,385 families in the tambon. In Nakhon Ratchasima, temperatures dipped to 15-17C in Phimai district, prompting teachers at Anuban Suriya Uthai Phimai School to organize outdoor activities to keep their students warm in the sun. Meanwhile, in Buri Ram, the temperature dropped to 13C in Pa Kham district, leading district chief Chaiwat Junthirapong to warn residents against lighting bonfires for warmth. Local authorities stepped in, distributing blankets to over 1,000 residents in need. The cold weather has truly taken its toll, underscoring the importance of community support during such trying times.

General Motors has recently announced a recall of 38,197 Chevrolet and Buick eAssist light hybrid cars due to a potential fire risk. The issue stems from circuit boards in the trunk that may overheat, leading to the 12-volt battery draining and warning lights illuminating. If these warning signs are ignored, the engine could stall, potentially resulting in a fire in the trunk. It is important to note that this issue is unrelated to the cars' lithium-ion battery that is part of the eAssist hybrid system. Most incidents have occurred within the first 1,000 miles of operation, prompting GM to take action. The automaker became aware of the issue in October 2012 and temporarily halted production to implement a fix. Cars built after December 2012 are not affected by the recall. Despite a trunk fire incident in March 2013, no injuries or crashes have been reported. Owners of the affected Chevrolet Malibu Eco and Buick LaCrosse and Regal sedans are urged to promptly bring their vehicles to the dealership upon noticing any warning lights. GM will be reaching out to owners to facilitate the necessary repairs.

Tunisia's deposed president Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali recounted a tale of betrayal and deceit, claiming he was lured away from his homeland to Saudi Arabia under false pretenses as his homeland embarks on a series of trials in his absence. In a statement released by his legal team on Monday, Ben Ali revealed that he boarded a plane bound for Saudi Arabia with the intent of ensuring his family's safety. However, he insisted that he had every intention of promptly returning to Tunisia. To his dismay, the aircraft's crew callously disregarded his pleas to wait for him, leaving him stranded in a foreign land. This dramatic turn of events transpired in January amidst widespread protests against his iron-fisted 23-year reign. The fallen leader now faces a litany of charges including embezzlement, money laundering, and drug trafficking in the current trial, with further legal proceedings on the horizon for offenses such as subversion and culpable homicide. A staggering 90 criminal cases loom over Ben Ali and his inner circle, with authorities vowing to prosecute him in both military and civilian courts. Despite vehemently denying any wrongdoing, Ben Ali remains out of reach in Saudi Arabia, where Tunisian authorities have been met with silence regarding extradition requests for him and his wife, Leila Trabelsi. The Tunisian populace, still reeling from the excesses of the former regime, has accused the erstwhile president and his kin of amassing illicit wealth through corrupt means. During the upheaval in January, enraged demonstrators ransacked and incinerated numerous businesses and opulent residences belonging to the Ben Ali clan. Ben Ali, refuting claims of his alleged vast riches, maintains his innocence in the face of mounting legal woes as the saga unfolds.
