BBC News reported that Uzbek troops have implemented strict measures to suppress dissent. Despite ongoing concerns about human rights violations in Uzbekistan, the European Union has decided to lift its arms embargo against the Central Asian nation. This embargo was initially imposed in 2005 following a tragic incident in which Uzbek government forces killed over 100 unarmed protesters in Andijan. EU foreign ministers have stated that the lifting of the embargo is intended to encourage Uzbek authorities to make improvements in the area of human rights. However, international human rights organizations have strongly criticized this decision. The EU had previously imposed sanctions on Uzbekistan in response to the government's refusal to allow for an international investigation into the events in Andijan. The recent decision to lift the arms embargo was made following Uzbekistan's release of political prisoners and abolition of the death penalty. The EU's move is believed to be influenced by Uzbekistan's strategic location in Central Asia, its abundant energy resources, and its assistance in supplying German troops in neighboring Afghanistan. EU foreign ministers have emphasized that they continue to have serious concerns about the human rights situation in Uzbekistan and have committed to reviewing the situation within a year. They have called on Uzbek authorities to release all imprisoned human rights activists, ensure freedom of speech, and combat child labor. Nonetheless, organizations such as Human Rights Watch and Amnesty International have criticized the decision to end sanctions, stating that it fails not only the victims of the Andijan massacre and their families but also numerous human rights defenders and journalists who continue to face harassment, torture, and detention in Uzbekistan today.

In the realm of digital marketing, the relentless pursuit of staying ahead in the game is a daily battle for marketers. The ever-evolving landscape demands constant vigilance, with new strategies, tactics, and tools emerging at a rapid pace. The deluge of information can easily overwhelm, turning the simple act of staying informed into a daunting task. In the face of a captivating article that beckons but time forbids a thorough read, one may resort to forwarding it to their email, saving it to bookmarks, or pinning it to a digital board. These were once my go-to solutions, until a revelation struck. After diligently collecting a trove of articles in my bookmarks folder over months as a wellspring of inspiration for an upcoming marketing strategy, I was dismayed to find upon revisiting them that many links had withered away into the void. Articles vanished, links morphed, leaving me grasping at the remnants of what was once a rich resource. Since that moment of realization, I have refined my approach, honing a method that ensures the preservation of valuable insights. And now, I shall impart this refined process unto you.

Originally known as Ta-Ra by the Gadigal people, Millers Point derived its current name from the windmills that once dotted its hills, owned by the infamous John Leighton, or Jack the Miller. Throughout the 19th century, this maritime enclave thrived as a hub of trade and industry, with its residents and employers intricately linked to the bustling wharves that lined its shores. However, the turn of the 20th century marked a pivotal moment in the area's history, as the outbreak of the bubonic plague prompted government intervention and the initiation of a massive redevelopment project. Despite this upheaval, Millers Point stood as a testament to resilience, witnessing the construction of iconic public works such as the Harbour Bridge and the expansion of wharves from Woolloomooloo to White Bay. Yet, the community's survival was once again put to the test in the 1970s, when the threat of high-rise development loomed large under the Askin government. It was in this moment of crisis that Jack Mundey and the Green Ban movement emerged as staunch defenders of the area's heritage, successfully preserving not only its historic buildings but also the livelihoods of its low-income residents. Thus, the battle for Millers Point transcended mere architectural conservation, embodying a larger struggle for social justice and the preservation of community identity in the face of relentless urbanization.

Unveiling a treasure trove of previously unseen footage, this special presentation delves into the early adventures of acclaimed naturalist David Attenborough in a way never before experienced - in vibrant colour. From the depths of the BBC's renowned film archives emerges the groundbreaking television series Zoo Quest, capturing the essence of Attenborough's pioneering work in a whole new light. Originally aired in December 1954, Zoo Quest quickly garnered widespread acclaim, propelling Attenborough into the spotlight as a distinguished wildlife presenter. Revolutionizing the way audiences perceived the natural world, the series showcased unprecedented footage of wildlife and indigenous communities previously unseen by human eyes. With the recent discovery of colour film footage, viewers can now witness the beauty and wonder of Zoo Quest to West Africa, Zoo Quest to Guiana, and Zoo Quest for a Dragon in breathtaking HD colour for the very first time. Delve into the fascinating behind-the-scenes accounts from Attenborough and cameraman Charles Lagus, as this exclusive presentation offers a captivating glimpse into the making of a television phenomenon that continues to captivate audiences worldwide.

Flacco's performance on Sunday night started off shaky, with two punts and an interception in his first three drives. However, he quickly found his stride and led the Ravens to three consecutive touchdowns. He showcased his skill with precise throws and smart decision-making, rebounding from his early mistakes. Flacco led crucial fourth-quarter scoring drives, including the game-winning field goal by Tucker. On the other hand, Schaub had a rough start with a safety on his first snap, but he too recovered and threw three touchdown passes on his next possessions. His long scoring throws demonstrated his accuracy and anticipation, aided by effective play-action fakes. Despite a gruesome injury, Schaub displayed resilience by returning to the game after just one play. His crucial connection with Johnson on a third down helped secure the victory for the Texans. Both quarterbacks showed determination and skill in overcoming adversity to lead their teams to success.

During his keynote address at the Eurogamer Expo, Microsoft corporate vice president Phil Harrison declared that the launch of the Xbox One on November 22 would mark the beginning of a "more than 10-year journey" for the platform. With a commitment to support the console through a variety of features and services, including the innovative use of cloud technology, Microsoft is poised to ensure the longevity and evolution of the Xbox One for years to come. In contrast, the Xbox 360, which debuted in November 2005, is set to be supported for at least three more years, according to Microsoft chief marketing and strategy officer Yusuf Mehdi. Harrison emphasized that the focus is not solely on the launch date, but on the ongoing improvement and adaptation of the console. With access to 300,000 dedicated servers, Microsoft is prepared to enhance the Xbox One with advanced features such as multiplayer capabilities, networking services, cloud processing, and artificial intelligence, setting the stage for a truly immersive and dynamic gaming experience.

According to Gallup's annual World Affairs survey, only 48 percent of Democrats sympathize more with Israelis than Palestinians in the tensions in the Middle East, compared to 83 percent of Republicans. Overall, 62 percent of Americans side with Israelis. However, these numbers don't tell the whole story. The support for Israelis among Democrats has actually increased significantly since the mid-1990s, as it has for Republicans. In the past year, there has been a ten-point drop in support for Israelis among Democrats, which is similar to the decline seen across all parties after the first Gulf War. The timing of the survey, conducted during the debate over Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's speech to Congress, may have influenced these results. The invitation and speech have been criticized for injecting partisan politics into the U.S.-Israel relationship, as reflected in Gallup's findings. Despite these fluctuations, overall support for Israel among Americans remains high, with 70 percent rating Israel favorably. This trend has been consistently on the rise since the 1990s.

A billowing cloud of dark smoke painted the sky, visible from far and wide, as witnesses recounted the sheer force of the explosion that sent several train carriages careening off the tracks. Ministry spokesperson Shota Utiashvili revealed that the blasts had occurred near an abandoned Georgian military base, where Russian troops had left behind a cache of munitions seized from the Georgian army upon their departure from Gori. Speculation arose that either the stockpile itself or the railway had been deliberately sabotaged by the Russian forces, though thankfully no casualties were reported. Georgian authorities had been diligently working to facilitate the return of numerous refugees to Gori, having recently completed a thorough mine-clearing operation in the town nestled near the border of the breakaway region of South Ossetia. Prime Minister Lado Gurgenidze emphasized the critical importance of the railway not only to Georgia's economy but also to the prosperity of neighboring nations, as the track meandered its way through the bustling capital of Tbilisi before branching out to the Black Sea ports of Poti and Batumi, and further southward toward the Turkish border. Among the wreckage, a single wagon bore the insignia of Azpetrol, a prominent company based in Baku, Azerbaijan. In light of the escalating conflict, President Sarkozy swiftly convened a special summit of EU leaders in Brussels on 1 September to address the pressing Georgian crisis, focusing on the future of EU-Russia relations and the provision of aid to Georgia. The conflict between Russia and Georgia had erupted into a four-day war following Tbilisi's ill-fated attempt to reclaim South Ossetia, a region that had declared independence in 1992 with Moscow's backing, culminating in a sudden offensive on 7 August amidst mounting tensions between Georgian and South Ossetian forces.

We are deeply troubled by the recent reports that have come to our attention. It is our firm belief that upholding the principles of net neutrality is paramount in ensuring that the Internet remains an open and unbiased platform, free from any form of interference by service providers without explicit consent from users. We are actively engaging with the relevant stakeholders to expedite a resolution to this matter. As brought to our attention by one of our esteemed blog readers, it appears that Rogers has once again implemented their content substitution tactic. A screenshot shared on Flickr depicts a warning issued by Rogers to a customer regarding the expiration of certain parental controls. This reemergence of content substitution raises significant apprehensions about Rogers' unauthorized tampering with the delivery of online content. Coupled with their persistent practice of redirecting unresolved web pages to company-sponsored paid search pages, it is evident that Rogers' proprietary content continues to be displayed without the requisite consent of end users on a recurring basis.

During discussions between Russian and UN officials, one of the conclusions reached was the need for the exiled government and rebels in Yemen to engage in dialogue and seek a political resolution. Additionally, there were talks on addressing the escalating humanitarian crisis in Yemen, with concerns raised about the possibility of a widespread famine. According to the UN, the conflict in Yemen, which began in March 2015 when Saudi Arabia intervened after Houthi rebels seized control of the capital Sana'a and ousted President Hadi, has resulted in the deaths of at least 10,000 people. Despite UN-led negotiations, a lasting ceasefire has yet to be achieved. Recent reports from the Houthi-controlled Saba news agency indicated that discussions took place between the charge d'affaires of the Russian Embassy in Yemen and the Houthi's minister of foreign affairs. Some supporters of the exiled Hadi government have accused Moscow of taking sides in the conflict, given Russia's criticism of Saudi Arabia's involvement in Yemen and its refusal to support UN resolutions calling for arms embargoes against the Houthi rebels. Former President Ali Abdullah Saleh has commended Russian President Vladimir Putin's approach to the Yemen conflict and referred to Russia as Yemen's "closest kin" on the global stage.

The series follows the story of a teenage boy and his family who have the ability to transform into werewolves, exploring themes of adolescence and societal acceptance. Departing slightly from the film version, the narrative is set in the fictional town of Wolverton, known for its history of werewolf sightings and attracting tourists. In contrast to the film, the protagonist Scott Howard's lycanthropic identity is kept hidden. Despite its target audience of young viewers, the animated series presents a poignant commentary on disability rights, portraying Scott's struggles with his "weird" feelings and physical transformations. While never causing harm as a werewolf, Scott grapples with his sense of otherness and navigates the town's prejudiced perceptions of his kind. Additionally, the character of Mick, a jock at Wolverton High, bullies Scott for his perceived outsider status.

In the tangled tapestry of the UK's dance with Europe, a saga unfolds. Episode one delves into the depths of history, uncovering the twists and turns that led to Britain's hesitant embrace of the Common Market. Decades of debate culminate in the looming shadow of a referendum, a weighty decision hanging in the balance. The corridors of power whisper secrets of past leaders, their choices shaping the course of a nation. From the initial rejection to the eventual embrace, the journey is fraught with triumphs and tribulations. Winston Churchill, Harold Macmillan, and Edward Heath stand as pivotal figures in this unfolding drama. Charles de Gaulle's rejection only fueled Heath's determination, leading the UK into the Common Market. Yet, the seeds of discord were already sown, paving the way for today's turbulent waters. Through a tapestry of interviews with key players - Tony Blair, David Cameron, Roy Jenkins, Enoch Powell, and more - a story of wit and poignancy emerges. The echoes of the past reverberate in the present, a reminder of the tangled web that binds us to our European neighbors.

Renowned American artist John H Wurdeman was initially captivated by the haunting melodies of Georgia's traditional folk music, leading him to embark on a journey to the heart of the former Soviet state. Sixteen years have passed since his arrival, yet he remains ensconced in a tapestry of culture steeped in time-honored traditions and raw emotions. Describing Georgia as a realm where "tears flow as freely as laughter rings true", this 37-year-old impressionist painter, a graduate of the esteemed Surikov Institute in Moscow, Russia, first set foot in the picturesque town of Signaghi in 1996, nestled amidst the vineyards of the country's renowned wine region. Residing alongside his wife Ketevan and their two children, Wurdeman has since established the acclaimed winery, Pheasant's Tears, dedicated to the preservation of Georgia's rich winemaking heritage. In a candid conversation with the BBC, he delves into his fervor for both art and wine, shedding light on the unique propensity of Georgians to openly express their deepest emotions to strangers. Crafted for the BBC by the talented Ilya Shnitser, this captivating narrative unveils the soul-stirring odyssey of an artist who has found his true calling amidst the enchanting landscapes of Georgia.

The parishioners of St Frances X Cabrini Church in Scituate, Massachusetts have fought an 11-year battle to keep their church open, but their efforts have ultimately ended in defeat. Despite maintaining an around-the-clock vigil with about 100 worshippers, the US Supreme Court's refusal to hear their final appeal against the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston's decision to close the church marked the end of their protest.

The emotional final service on Sunday was described as a "celebration of faith and transition", as many parishioners shared embraces and shed tears. As the service concluded, quilts representing each year of the vigil were solemnly taken down from the church walls and carried out of the church, symbolizing the end of an era.

The decision to close St Frances X Cabrini and more than 75 other parishes was made due to declining attendances, a shortage of clergy, and deteriorating buildings. These closures were further exacerbated by the child sex abuse scandals that plagued the archdiocese. Despite the parishioners' decade-long fight and legal challenges that reached the Vatican, the archdiocese's legal ownership of the property ultimately allowed them to evict the protesters.

While the parishioners' battle may have come to an end, it is clear that their faith and sense of community remain strong. The archdiocese has expressed hope that the protesters will find solace in attending another church within the district.

As the world watches in awe, a brave cameraman captured the raw power of Iceland's Bardarbunga volcano, showcasing fountains of lava shooting an incredible 70 meters into the sky. The spectacle is accompanied by billowing clouds of smoke, a mixture of vapor and gas rather than the dangerous ash that poses a threat to air travel. Since the seismic activity began on August 16, a series of earthquakes have rattled the region, causing fractures in the Vatnajokull glacier to the northeast of the volcano. These fissures have allowed rivers of molten lava to flow freely, creating a mesmerizing yet ominous sight. The alert level for the area remains at orange, signifying an escalating level of unrest with the potential for a catastrophic eruption. Experts fear that the expanding lava flow could breach the southern boundaries of the glacier, leading to a catastrophic eruption beneath the ice. Such an event would trigger massive floods and violent explosions, spewing volcanic ash far and wide. Over the past 72 hours, the volcanic activity has intensified, with the lava now covering an area exceeding four square kilometers. The eruption site lies approximately 28 miles from the main Bardarbunga volcano, nestled beneath the vast Vatnajokull glacier that dominates Iceland's eastern landscape. Despite its remote and sparsely populated nature, the area is a popular destination for hikers during the summer months. In response to the escalating seismic activity, officials have evacuated all tourists from the region, prioritizing their safety above all else.

CD Projekt Red has recently rolled out an Xbox One X patch for The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, introducing two new graphical modes: Performance and 4K. In the 4K mode, the game is locked at a 4K resolution with a steady 30 frame-rate, while the performance mode allows for variable resolution and aims for a smoother 60 frames-per-second experience. This means that the game will adjust its resolution dynamically, ranging from 1080p to 4K. Both modes also include support for HDR, with a forthcoming patch for the PS4 Pro expected to add HDR functionality. The update also incorporates improved shadows, ambient occlusion, texture filtering, and higher resolution textures. To access the new graphics modes on the Xbox One X, players can navigate to the game's Options menu, Display, and then Advanced settings.

Researchers from China and Singapore have utilized electrospinning to create a standalone catalyst for producing hydrogen and oxygen on a large scale. The process of electrocatalysis is essential in water splitting devices for oxygen reduction and hydrogen evolution. While platinum-based catalysts are effective, they are expensive and not very long-lasting, which limits their widespread use. Electrospinning, however, offers a solution by producing fibres that can be used to manufacture scalable electrocatalysts. One challenge with these catalysts has been their limited number of active sites and inefficient mass transport pathways. But now, a team led by Shengjie Peng from the National University of Singapore and Xiaohong Qin from Donghua University has found a breakthrough. They have developed porous, channel-rich carbon nanofibres using a blend of pyrolysed electrospun polyacrylonitrile and cellulose acetate nanofibres. During the synthesis, the decomposition of cellulose acetate created the much-needed active sites and mass transport pathways, enhancing the catalytic performance. In addition, the team added iron-based precursors to the spinning solution as cost-effective and efficient electrocatalysts. With the new material, Peng and his colleagues successfully created a flexible and stable 180 x 80cm electrocatalyst with impressive performance. This innovation is expected to pave the way for the next generation of flexible electrodes.

We expand the concept of phase transformations to encompass periodic cellular materials by introducing materials with unit cells housing multiple stable configurations. Each stable configuration of the unit cell represents a distinct phase, and transitions between these phases are considered phase transformations within the cellular material. By showcasing a cellular material that showcases phase transformation, we highlight the crucial elements of unit cell geometry that drive its mechanical properties and introduce an analytical model elucidating its constitutive behavior. Notably, cellular materials undergoing phase transformations exhibit hysteresis, manifesting as prolonged serrated loading and unloading plateaus, rendering them particularly well-suited for energy absorption applications. Unlike traditional metal and polymeric honeycombs, these phase-transforming cellular materials offer comparable energy absorption performance alongside fully recoverable deformation, marking a significant advancement in material design and functionality.

Medical marijuana became a topic of discussion that transcended party lines during Tuesday night's Senate debate in Louisiana. Senator Mary Landrieu, the Democratic incumbent, took a firm stance against the use of marijuana for medical purposes, while her Republican challenger, Representative Bill Cassidy, a respected doctor, voiced his support for its use. This partisan divide stood out as somewhat unusual, considering that traditionally, states leaning towards the Democratic party have been more receptive to the idea of medical marijuana compared to their Republican-leaning counterparts. Despite Landrieu's opposition to medical marijuana, an interesting observation was made by BuzzFeed's Andrew Kaczynski regarding her apparent acceptance of keg stands on college campuses. This was highlighted when a photo surfaced of the senator assisting a man in his late 20s with a keg stand at a Louisiana State University tailgating event in September, as reported by the Hill. It is worth noting that excessive alcohol consumption is a significant concern, with nearly one in 10 deaths among Americans aged 20 to 64 attributed to it, as per a report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention published in June. In contrast, marijuana has never been linked to a fatal overdose, although it may pose an increased risk of being involved in traffic accidents.

Winger David Worrall's stunning free-kick proved to be the difference as Southend kept their dreams of automatic promotion alive with a crucial victory over Bury. The former Bury player's 25-yard curler leveled the points with Wycombe Wanderers in third place. Bury had their chances with Tom Soares, Joe Riley, and Danny Rose coming close, but the home side couldn't find the back of the net despite the overwhelming support of over 8,000 fans who were granted free entry. The match was a highly anticipated one after the original fixture was abandoned due to heavy rain, attracting the club's largest home crowd in nearly two decades.

Although Bury dominated the first half, Southend fought back and substitute Worrall's goal in the 74th minute, following Kelvin Etuhu's foul on Jack Payne, sealed the victory. Bury had a late opportunity to equalize through Nathan Cameron's header, but it went wide, and goalkeeper Daniel Bentley's heroics denied Ryan Lowe to secure Southend's seventh consecutive clean sheet.

Enter AndroidWorks, a dazzling gateway to the world of game development on Android. Get ready to embark on a thrilling journey of innovation and creativity with AndroidWorks – the dawn of a new era in game development on Android devices.

The New York Giants are set to sign free-agent quarterback Geno Smith, according to reports from ESPN's Adam Schefter and Jordan Raanan. Smith is expected to undergo a physical with the team this weekend and is likely to sign on Monday pending any medical concerns, as per a source cited by Schefter. If he has fully recovered from an ACL tear sustained in October, Smith will rejoin former New York Jets teammate Brandon Marshall as a backup to Eli Manning. Smith started 29 games for the Jets in his first two seasons but famously lost his starting position before the 2015 season following a broken jaw incident involving then-teammate IK Enemkpali. The 26-year-old has only started one game in the past two years, during Week 7 of last season, before suffering an ACL injury after throwing just eight passes.

An Indonesian diplomat stationed in Saudi Arabia has expressed dismay over the decision to overturn the conviction of a Saudi woman who was found guilty of beating and torturing her Indonesian maid. Didi Wahyudi, speaking to the BBC, emphasized that the initial three-year prison sentence was considered a significant ruling, but with the recent overturning of the verdict, there is now a lack of accountability for perpetrators of such crimes. Saudi Arabia has not issued a statement on the matter. 

A substantial number of Indonesian women are employed in Saudi households, and many have reported instances of mistreatment by their employers. Recent events, including the arrest of two individuals in Mecca in connection with the tragic death of their Indonesian maid, highlight the prevalence of abuse faced by migrant domestic workers in Saudi Arabia. Despite several cases coming to light in recent years, offenders have seldom faced severe repercussions, often receiving only fines as punishment.

The case of Sumiati Binti Salan Mustapa, a 23-year-old maid who was hospitalized with severe injuries in November, attracted global attention and prompted Indonesian President to urge for justice in her case. In January, her 53-year-old female employer was sentenced to three years in prison by a Medina court. However, the employer successfully appealed the verdict and was acquitted due to purported lack of evidence. Didi Wahyudi, representing the Indonesian consulate in Saudi Arabia, lamented the outcome, stating that the original ruling could have set a precedent for holding abusers accountable. He expressed concern over the implications of the overturned verdict, noting that it sets a troubling precedent where perpetrators of such heinous acts go unpunished.

Pakistan's interior minister is not mincing words with the radical Islamists who have been causing a ruckus in central Islamabad for the past four days. Chaudhry Nisar Ali Khan has given them a clear ultimatum: pack up and go home peacefully within hours, or face the consequences. The tension has been building since Sunday, when over 10,000 members of Pakistan's Sunni Tehreek group stormed the capital to protest the hanging of Mumtaz Qadri for the murder of Gov. Salman Taseer. Now, the once massive crowd has dwindled to just 1,200 die-hard protesters. Their demands include the execution of a Christian woman Taseer defended against blasphemy accusations. It seems like the government's patience is wearing thin, and things could get messy if the protesters don't listen up.

Upon learning of this relationship, Rajesh Mavi, a prominent and affluent figure in the area, allegedly dispatched a group of individuals to abduct Robin. Subsequently, the victim was taken to Rajesh's property in the Tila-Shahbazpur region, where he was subjected to sexual assault, attacked by dogs, and subjected to further physical harm with the application of salt and chili, as per law enforcement. The perpetrators proceeded to share explicit images on social media using a fabricated account, prompting Robin's family to intervene and rescue their son, despite facing threats of reprisal. The United States has deployed additional medical personnel to Guantanamo Bay in response to a hunger strike among detainees at the facility. Approximately 40 nurses and specialists arrived over the weekend, according to camp spokesman Lt Col Samuel House. Currently, 100 out of 166 detainees are participating in the hunger strike, with 21 of them being force-fed through a tube. The protest stems from the detainees' objection to their indefinite detention, as most are being held without charge. This hunger strike, which began in February, has gained momentum in recent weeks and is one of the longest and most widespread in Guantanamo's history. While some reports suggest the strike was triggered by alleged mishandling of the Koran during cell searches, Guantanamo officials deny these claims. An incident of violence occurred on April 13 when authorities moved inmates out of communal cellblocks where surveillance cameras and windows had been covered. Some inmates used improvised weapons, prompting a response with "less-than-lethal rounds" from camp officials; fortunately, no serious injuries were reported. Despite nearly 100 detainees having been cleared for release, they remain at the facility due to restrictions imposed by Congress and concerns of potential mistreatment if they are repatriated. Guantanamo Bay was established in 2002 to house individuals captured in counter-terrorism operations following the 9/11 attacks in the United States.

CPython employs reference counting as a method to manage an object's liveness, a widely utilized strategy that is relatively straightforward to implement. However, navigating reference counting within the CPython API can prove to be a cumbersome task for those unfamiliar with it. The CPython API introduces complexities to reference counting, with references being categorized as new, borrowed, stolen, or copied depending on their usage within the C API. Functions in the API return new and borrowed references, each requiring specific actions from the programmer. New references signify ownership and necessitate manual decrementing of the reference count, while borrowed references necessitate incrementing the count if the object needs to be retained. On the other hand, stolen and copied references are passed as arguments to functions, with stolen references relieving the programmer of responsibility for decrementing the count, while copied references still require manual management. While CPython streamlines reference counting to some extent by determining the behavior of functions, the intricacies of managing reference counts can still complicate the programming process. Despite efforts to automate reference count management for users, the multitude of potential side effects on reference counts introduced by various functions leads to a proliferation of possibilities that can be difficult to navigate and troubleshoot. Despite diligent efforts to address reference count bugs, uncertainties persist regarding the complete resolution of such issues.

As the world's gaze fixated on Turkey's pivotal referendum vote this past Sunday, a lone Wikipedia user seized the opportunity to launch a pointed critique at Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, whose authority stands to be solidified with a victorious "yes" vote. In a bold stroke of defiance, the user opened the English-language Wikipedia article on Erdogan with a brazen declaration, labeling the Turkish leader as a dictator. Though swiftly expunged, the digital denouncement now locked from further alteration by unregistered users for a period of no less than one week, the mark had been made. The entry for President Erdogan, frozen in time at approximately 20:00 UTC on April 16th, bore witness to this fleeting act of digital rebellion.

Yet, this solitary act of dissent finds resonance in a chorus of disapproval that has crescendoed against Erdogan in recent times. In the wake of the thwarted military coup of July 2016, Turkey has languished under a state of emergency that has garnered sharp rebuke from global leaders, casting its shadow over the nation's democratic facade. The emergency decree has granted sweeping powers to the Turkish government, enabling the dismissal of swathes of state personnel and prolonging the detention of suspects without due process. Over a hundred thousand individuals, spanning the ranks of soldiers, law enforcement officers, and educators, have found themselves abruptly ousted from their positions since the inception of this draconian measure.

The aftermath of last year's coup attempt has seen a wave of arrests, with at least 40,000 individuals detained on suspicions of affiliations with US-based cleric Fethullah Gulen, whom Turkey accuses of masterminding the failed insurrection. Against this backdrop of political turmoil, Sunday's referendum looms large, poised to consolidate Erdogan's authority in a manner that would grant him unchecked dominion over the nation's fiscal matters, the dissolution of parliament, and the unilateral appointment and dismissal of government officials and jurists, free from the scrutiny of parliamentary oversight.

Following the announcement by BlackBerry that it would cease production of its own smartphones, concerns arose regarding the fate of the company's renowned QWERTY keyboards. However, CEO John Chen allayed these fears during an interview with BNN, affirming that BlackBerry intends to introduce another smartphone featuring a physical keyboard in the foreseeable future. While the company will persist in developing smartphones with QWERTY keyboards, it is conceivable that the design of the keyboard may undergo modifications. BlackBerry must uphold the distinctive style and superior craftsmanship associated with its physical keyboards, even if the actual construction and design is outsourced. Although there is no definitive timeline for the release of the next BlackBerry device with a physical keyboard, it is imperative that the company ensures meticulous attention to detail in the manufacturing process.

The Australian Medical Association has supported a Canberra GP's proposal to safeguard neighbors of public housing tenants from secondhand smoke. Dr. Stephen Moulding's plea for action was prompted by numerous complaints from patients at his Narrabundah clinic, both private and public residents, regarding the harmful smoke from adjacent public tenants infiltrating their homes. With 40 years of experience as a GP, Dr. Moulding has encountered many patients who have expressed concerns about second-hand smoke from public housing tenants residing on small blocks. He emphasized the need for a compromise to protect residents and children from involuntary exposure to secondhand smoke, without necessarily advocating for a complete ban on smoking in public housing. One of his patients recounted to Fairfax Media that the doors and windows of her two-story duplex, including those of her 9-year-old son's bedroom, had to remain closed at all times due to a public tenant smoking in the front yard, which was less than two meters away.

China's top land and resources regulator announced on Saturday plans to establish a bureau dedicated to real estate registration in order to streamline property management reform efforts. Vice Minister Xu Deming emphasized the importance of this initiative at a work-planning meeting, stating that the bureau will play a key role in implementing a unified system for registration. This system will encompass regulations, registration processes, information services, documentation, and survey standards. Additionally, China aims to expedite rural land property surveying and registration, as well as advance the stockholding system reform in rural areas. Vice Minister Xu suggested that smaller cities and towns prioritize real estate registration in their organizational and governmental reforms, while larger cities should collaborate with relevant departments and share best practices. Ultimately, the establishment of a comprehensive real estate registration system is crucial for the potential implementation of a property tax in China.

According to a reliable source, YouTube Connect offers similar features to Periscope and Facebook Live. Users can easily log in with their Google or YouTube account and start streaming from their mobile devices. The app includes chat and tagging functions, as well as a "news feed" featuring the latest videos from friends or subscribed channels. Additionally, videos can be viewed on the YouTube Connect app or the YouTube website. The app also allows streamers to archive previous broadcasts for viewers to watch later. While YouTube has allowed live streaming for some time, YouTube Connect appears to be a new approach to spontaneous streaming, which has become popular with the rise of Periscope.

Calgary police are seeking assistance from the public in locating three individuals wanted in connection with a stolen vehicle investigation conducted earlier this year. Operation Incessant, which spanned two weeks in January and February, targeted individuals involved in the theft of vehicles left unattended throughout the city. In the aftermath of the covert operation, seven suspects were charged with a total of 24 criminal offenses. Presently, authorities are actively searching for three suspects who are the subjects of a total of 28 warrants. One of the individuals, Anastassios Tasso Siokas, aged 49 and a resident of Calgary, is currently wanted on 12 warrants for various offenses including obstruction of a peace officer, impersonation, driving while disqualified, possession of a stolen credit card, and possession of stolen property. Siokas is described as being white, standing at five feet 10 inches, having a medium build, brown eyes, and partially gray hair. The other two suspects, Ian Edward Morris, 27, and Sage Bryanna Bartman, 21, have had warrants issued for their arrest in March. Individuals with pertinent information are urged to contact the police at 403-266-1234 or provide anonymous tips to Crime Stoppers.

In a court in eastern China, three activists received jail terms of up to six and a half years as part of a civil rights movement advocating for government officials to publicly disclose their assets. The sentences, deemed excessive by their supporters, reveal the increasingly stringent stance taken by China's Communist party against political dissent, regardless of its peaceful expression or loose organization. Party leaders have been vigilant of any independent social force with the potential to threaten their rule, seeking to suppress the loosely knit New Citizens movement to which the activists belonged. The district court in Xinyu imposed six and a half-year sentences on labor activist Liu Ping and Wei Zhongping, while fellow activist Li Sihua received three years. Their lawyer, Zhou Ze, asserted that the activists were convicted of "creating a disturbance," a vaguely defined offense that has been increasingly used to detain activists. Their convictions, particularly those of Liu and Wei, were deemed unjust by their lawyer Si Weijiang, who argued that there was no legal basis for the charges. The heavier sentences imposed on Liu and Wei, compared to the four-year sentence of the group's founder Xu Zhiyong, and the broader crackdown on political expression since last spring, reflect a concerted effort by the authorities to silence political dissidents.

As anticipated and widely anticipated, Isil initiated a deliberate act of arson at the Mishraq Chemical plant and sulphur mine located 30 km south of Mosul on the preceding Thursday while retreating towards the city. The resultant consequences have been grave, with a reported death toll of up to nine individuals and approximately 1,000 individuals sustaining injuries, including foreign correspondents. The emanation of a toxic cloud, comprising highly hazardous substances such as sulphur dioxide and hydrogen sulphide, intermingled with remnants from ignited oil wells, poses a severe risk to individuals exposed without protective gear or shelter. Presently extending 20-30 km southward across sparsely populated terrain, the direction of the wind may potentially shift towards the east, a common occurrence during this season, imperiling the Kurdish capital Erbil situated 60 km away.

When considering cooking pots and pans, the selection of the appropriate size is a crucial factor to take into account. Smaller boiling pots are ideal for preparing meals for a small group and are convenient for transportation, even during extensive outdoor excursions. Conversely, larger boiling pots are indispensable when hosting gatherings and ensuring ample food supply for a sizable number of guests. Cast-iron cookware is a resilient choice that excels in outdoor cooking settings. Additionally, aluminum and stainless-steel pot kits offer versatility in culinary preparations. Aluminum pot kits provide essential tools for frying poultry or fish, including a thermometer for precise cooking temperatures and a marinade injector for enhancing flavors. Stainless-steel pot kits often come equipped with a strainer or lifter for effortless food removal while minimizing oil splatter. Explore our range of fryers to discover additional options for creating delectable dishes that will leave your guests clamoring for more.

Valve boss Gabe Newell's recognition as a fellow of the British Academy of Film and Television Arts for his exceptional contributions to the video game industry is a well-deserved honor. Through the creation of influential titles such as Half Life, Team Fortress 2, and DOTA 2, Valve has played a pivotal role in nurturing a vibrant gaming community. What sets Newell and Valve apart is not just their ability to develop groundbreaking games, but their dedication to empowering players to become creators through modding tools. This unique approach has not only enriched the gaming experience but also fostered a sense of collaboration and innovation within the industry. The acknowledgment of Newell's impact by the Bafta video games committee further solidifies his status as a pioneer in the field. Additionally, Valve's commitment to expanding gaming accessibility through initiatives like the Steam box demonstrates their ongoing dedication to pushing boundaries and reaching new audiences. In a line-up of esteemed industry fellows like Peter Molyneux, Shigeru Miyamoto, and Will Wright, Gabe Newell's induction stands as a testament to his lasting legacy and influence in shaping the future of gaming.

Liam Geddes, a talented producer hailing from Milton Keynes, has been making waves in the music scene since 2013 with his releases on esteemed imprints like MIL, Pathway Tracks, and Love Not Money. Now, he is stepping into a new chapter as he launches the fresh imprint Dailycid, joining forces with Romanian newcomer Marius Laurentiu. Geddes brings his signature funky and functional touch to the table with tracks like "For The Time It Took," a seductive vocal house anthem with a deep bassline and infectious rhythms that are sure to ignite any dancefloor. On the other hand, "Ceviche" takes a smoother, lounge-inspired approach reminiscent of early Cassio. Meanwhile, Laurentiu showcases his talent with the mesmerizing and ethereal journey of "Black Sea Pink Sky," proving once again why Romanian producers are hailed as some of the best in the industry. This track stands shoulder to shoulder with works by esteemed artists like Andrei Ciubuc and Sepp, showcasing a level of artistry and creativity that is truly exceptional.

The recent arrest of two brothers in Belgium in connection with an anti-terror operation has sent shockwaves through the country. The charges brought against one of the brothers, Nourredine H, for attempting to commit "terrorist murder" and being part of a terrorist group, have heightened fears of further attacks in the region. The absence of weapons or explosives found in the searches may provide some relief, but the uncertainty surrounding the organisation Nourredine H is accused of working for leaves a lingering sense of unease. Belgium, still reeling from the tragic bombings in Brussels earlier this year, remains on edge as authorities work tirelessly to prevent any future threats. The increased security measures ahead of the national holiday on 21 July are a stark reminder of the ever-present danger posed by extremist ideologies. The possibility of an attack similar to the tragedy in Nice serves as a sobering reminder of the constant threat faced by innocent civilians in today's volatile world.

Democrats and progressives fervently believe that the Citizens United decision has left a devastating mark on our nation, akin to the infamous Dred Scott ruling. As Hillary Clinton delivered her concession speech in New Hampshire, the gravity of this Supreme Court decision was underscored. With unwavering conviction, she lamented the fact that the ruling prevented the legal suppression of a documentary that criticized her, all because the entity behind it was a corporation. In a moment charged with emotion, she boldly declared, "Citizens United, one of the worst Supreme Court decisions in our country's history, was actually a case about a right-wing attack on me and my campaign. A right-wing organization took aim at me and ended up damaging our entire democracy." The passion in her voice was palpable as she vowed to fight for campaign finance reform, emphasizing the need to rid politics of secret, unaccountable money. This recurring narrative from Clinton, painting the expansion of free political speech as a personal affront, speaks volumes about the contentious nature of American politics today. The underlying message is clear: politicians seeking to control and restrict the ability of Americans to voice dissent. It's a chilling notion, but in the current landscape of American politics, perhaps not entirely unexpected.

Walt Disney's beloved character, Dumbo, faced ridicule and rejection due to his oversized ears, a result of a mix-up by the baby-delivery stork. Dumbo, actually intended to be an African elephant, possesses ears proportionate to his species, which are notably larger than those of Asian elephants. The distinct shape of the ears mirrors the continents of Africa and India. The film's narrative underscores themes of resilience and overcoming adversity, resonating with audiences of all ages. For those interested, an article in Open Exchange Magazine delves into the inspirational message of Dumbo. A new DVD release, Dumbo: Big Top Edition, offers a fresh viewing experience, evoking emotional responses that touch the soul. Whether revisiting the classic film or discovering it for the first time, viewers are in for a moving and uplifting experience.

In the realm of feline delight, a mysterious allure beckons many a curious cat towards the humble olive. Within its savory flesh lies a secret potion, a shimmering elixir of isoprenoids that whispers of ancient magic. These compounds, akin to the essence of catnip, dance within the pimentos and Kalamata greens, weaving a spell that captivates the senses. As the molecules caress the receptors in the feline's delicate vomeronasal organ, a symphony of pleasure cascades through their being, igniting a fire of fascination. In this moment, even the most stoic of cats may succumb to the olive's enchantment, revealing a side unseen. Yet, not all whiskered companions are swayed by this emerald temptress, for each soul dances to its own tune. And though the olive may offer little in terms of sustenance, it is but a fleeting indulgence in the grand tapestry of a cat's world. As the wise whispers of Jackson Galaxy and Tracie Hotchner echo through the corridors of feline fancy, we are reminded that true enrichment lies not in the fruit of the olive, but in the playful pursuit of hidden treasures that spark joy within the heart of our beloved companions.

The United States will commence operations of its premier fighter aircraft, the F-22 Raptor, from bases in northern Australia starting next year. This significant revelation was made by Admiral Harry Harris, the highest-ranking American military official in the Pacific, during his visit to Sydney. In emphasizing the importance of projecting strength to deter potential aggression in the region, Admiral Harris underscored the unwavering commitment of the United States to maintain a leading role in the Asia-Pacific area. He emphasized that the nation's strategic interests are enduring and will not be altered by the change in leadership on January 20th, alluding to the inauguration of President Donald Trump. Admiral Harris further disclosed that an agreement has been formalized for Australia to host US military assets, notably the formidable F-22 Raptors, renowned as the world's premier fighter aircraft. This development is expected to serve as a robust demonstration of US military presence and commitment in the region, signaling a positive step forward in bolstering security and stability.

In a recent development, Boston Dynamics has unveiled the next generation of its renowned sprinting robot, dubbed WildCat, which has surpassed its predecessor, the "Cheetah," in terms of capabilities. Unlike the previous model, WildCat is no longer tethered to offboard hydraulic pumps for power, allowing it to freely navigate flat terrain with impressive speeds of up to 16mph, as demonstrated in a video released by the company. The power source for WildCat has been revealed to be a 2-stroke go-kart engine directly linked to a hydraulic pump, enabling it to operate for approximately five minutes on a small fuel tank to maintain a lightweight design. This advancement in robotics technology raises concerns about the potential implications for the future, as the efficiency and endurance of WildCat remain uncertain.

Two Egyptians were tragically killed and two others injured in a devastating attack on a Coptic church near Misrata, Libya. The incident, which occurred while the victims were having lunch, involved an explosion at the church building. The perpetrator behind the blast remains unknown, and conflicting reports have emerged regarding the timing of the attack. The discovery of home-made dynamite at the scene suggests a deliberate act of violence. The Egyptian government has called for increased security measures at the church and has urged for a thorough investigation to bring those responsible to justice. This incident highlights the challenges faced by Libya in maintaining stability and security following the overthrow of Gaddafi, with a rise in attacks targeting various religious and diplomatic institutions.

South Sydney's CEO, John Lee, has issued a call to action for an immediate reassessment of the NRL's recent interpretation of the shoulder charge rule. This comes as Rabbitohs hooker Issac Luke prepares to challenge his charge at the judiciary, potentially setting a precedent for future cases. Luke, already admitting guilt to a dangerous-throw charge, could face a three-match suspension if unsuccessful. However, a successful challenge would only see him miss the upcoming clash with Canterbury. The team is further impacted as five-eighth Luke Keary has been ruled out of the match after pleading guilty to a similar charge. These incidents highlight the growing confusion surrounding the shoulder charge rule, with recent suspensions including Manly's Willie Mason. The NRL's decision to redefine the shoulder charge criteria has sparked debate and raised questions about consistency and fairness in the judiciary process.

I am thrilled to hear that Mauro Tassotti has decided to remain with AC Milan as a scout. As a longtime fan of the club, I have always admired Tassotti's dedication and passion for the team. It was disheartening to see him initially part ways with the club earlier this summer, but I am glad that he has found a new role within the organization. His 35-year relationship with the club speaks volumes about his commitment and knowledge of the team. I believe that his experience and expertise will be invaluable in identifying and nurturing talent within the Milan ranks. I am excited to see how Tassotti's new role will contribute to the future success of the team.

Authorities in eastern Canada are advising individuals to consider avoiding consumption of romaine lettuce due to an ongoing E. coli outbreak that has resulted in one fatality and 40 reported illnesses. Quebec and Newfoundland and Labrador have each confirmed 13 cases, with Ontario reporting 8, New Brunswick 5, and Nova Scotia 1. The Public Health Agency of Canada has linked the cases of E. coli 0157 to the consumption of romaine lettuce. Additionally, ten more cases have been reported, and the investigation into the outbreak remains ongoing. The agency assures that the public health notice will be regularly updated as the investigation progresses. The affected individuals range in age from four to 80, with 70 percent of those affected being female.
