Pads reaching for the edge, a bold declaration of independence. Lazy, perhaps, but in the rush of inspiration, time is a luxury I cannot afford. Routing single-sided boards, a dance of precision and passion. 1206 zero ohm resistors, 6 mil traces, a symphony of design. Vias like stars scattered across the night sky, guiding me on my journey of creation. A masterpiece in the making, a diamond in the rough, waiting to shine with the brilliance of a thousand suns. Let us create something truly special, a melody that will echo through the ages.

In the rugged terrain of north-eastern Colombia, tragedy struck with the unforgiving force of an explosion, claiming the lives of two valiant soldiers and an innocent eight-year-old boy. The sinister hand of Colombia's largest left-wing rebel group, the Farc, had cunningly planted the explosives that ripped through the peaceful town of Tame. Amidst the chaos and devastation, three soldiers were left wounded, a stark reminder of the unpredictable dangers that lurk in this war-torn region. Colombian Defence Minister Juan Carlos Pinzon, with a steely resolve, acknowledged the escalating security crisis that has plagued the country in recent months, yet vowed to confront the looming threat with unwavering determination. This heinous act unfolded in the very same area where just days prior, nine workers from an oil company were snatched from their daily lives, their fate hanging precariously in the balance. The murky shadows of uncertainty shroud the identity of the perpetrators, as the lawless underworld of Arauca province teems with a labyrinth of illicit groups vying for control. Despite the Farc's recent pledge to cease ransom kidnappings, the menacing presence of the ELN and ruthless drug cartels continues to cast a dark pall over the region, perpetuating a cycle of violence and fear. A poignant reminder of the harrowing realities faced by the innocent populace came in the form of a young girl, abducted on her way to school and held captive for 18 agonizing days before the compassionate intervention of the International Red Cross secured her release. The enduring legacy of the Marxist-inspired Farc, born in the turbulent era of the 1960s, remains a formidable force, its influence fueled by the illicit proceeds of the drug trade and a dogged resilience in the face of relentless military offensives. As the nation grapples with the specter of violence and unrest, the echoes of tragedy serve as a somber reminder of the fragile peace that hangs in the balance.

The Supreme Court has announced that it will review an appellate ruling upholding bans on same-sex marriage in four states to determine if same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide. The case is scheduled to be argued in April with a decision expected by late June. Currently, 14 states, including Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and Tennessee, do not permit same-sex marriage, but the number of states allowing it has nearly doubled in the past three months. The Supreme Court's decision to not hear same-sex marriage appeals in October allowed some rulings to take effect, resulting in Florida becoming the 36th state to issue marriage licenses to same-sex couples last week.

Are you yearning for the tantalizing tang of sour gummy candies? With just a few basic ingredients from the store, you can easily whip up these delectable delights in the comfort of your own kitchen. These lip-smacking gummies can be customized to suit your taste buds, with a rainbow of flavors and colors to choose from. For an extra punch of sourness, go ahead and add a full packet of Kool-Aid to the mix. And for those looking to cut back on sugar, simply opt for sugar-free Jell-O. The beauty of creating your own sour gummy candies lies in the endless possibilities for creativity - experiment with whimsical shapes using candy molds of all varieties. If molds are not on hand, fear not! A pan, ice cube tray, or any silicone mold will do the trick just fine. Let your imagination run wild as you craft these homemade treats that are sure to bring a burst of joy to your taste buds.

Sony faced criticism and backlash over the holidays as their PlayStation Network fell victim to a crippling denial-of-service attack orchestrated by Lizard Squad. After a nerve-wracking few days, the gaming service finally managed to bounce back. To make amends for the disruption during the festive season, Sony has decided to offer players a generous five-day extension on their PSN subscription and a special one-time 10 percent discount in the PSN store. The much-awaited UK code, T6R3KB529K, has been released today and will remain valid until 9am on January 26th. This code can be applied towards the total value of your PS3 or PS4 purchases, with a few exceptions such as video rentals, game pre-orders, and subscriptions to PS Plus and Music Unlimited. Despite these limitations, the code still presents an opportunity to stock up on digital games to keep you entertained until the highly anticipated release of Evolve next month. For those residing outside the UK, additional codes can be found on Sony's official website.

Researchers have utilized Fermi to detect gamma ray bursts originating from the far side of the Sun, a feat previously impossible. By aligning ultraviolet imagery captured by NASA's STEREO satellites with the gamma rays emitted from the opposite side, scientists were able to connect the dots and track the movement of particles traveling at an astonishing speed of 1,000 miles per second. These groundbreaking discoveries are set to expand our understanding of the universe, with implications for our knowledge of black hole formation and solar activity. The existence of blazars challenges conventional theories, while the observation of solar flares provides a clearer insight into the behavior of our Sun. Fermi, despite its limitations, has achieved remarkable feats since its launch in 2008, pushing the boundaries of our understanding of the cosmos.

Renowned Reuters photographer Goran Tomasevic recently immersed himself once again in the chaotic and dangerous landscape of Syria, where he courageously followed the Free Syrian Army through the war-torn streets of Damascus. In a particularly intense 24-hour period, Tomasevic found himself at the heart of the conflict, documenting the harrowing moments of an FSA attack mission. His lens captured the stark brutality of war as he witnessed the tragic death of a rebel at the hands of a government sniper, only to narrowly escape a tank shell explosion moments later. Through Tomasevic's lens, viewers are confronted with the raw and immediate horrors of urban warfare in Syria, serving as a poignant reminder of the ongoing violence and suffering in the region. However, these gripping images, while powerful, offer just a glimpse into the vast and complex reality of the prolonged and bloody uprising in Syria. Tomasevic's work underscores the importance of bearing witness to the human cost of conflict and the urgent need for global attention and action to address the ongoing crisis in Syria.

The resolute determination of Arsenal striker Nicklas Bendtner to uplift his own fortunes mirrors the ebb and flow of nature's beauty. Just as the seasons change and transform the landscape with their exquisite palette of colors, Bendtner's journey has seen moments of triumph and despair. His resurgence in late 2013, akin to the blooming of a rare flower, was followed by a tumultuous 2014 marked by setbacks and challenges. Like a lone tree standing tall in a storm, Bendtner faced adversity with a goal against Cardiff City on New Year's Day, only to be sidelined by injury. As the winds of fate shifted, he found himself overshadowed by the emergence of young talent and embroiled in controversy. Yet, like a phoenix rising from the ashes, Bendtner perseveres, pouring his heart and soul into grueling training sessions in a quest for redemption. The uncertainty of his future, much like the changing seasons, hangs in the balance, awaiting the next chapter in his poetic journey of resilience and determination.

Fourteen lives were tragically lost in a devastating blast that rocked a metro train in the bustling Russian city of St. Petersburg. As the dust settled and the shock of the attack reverberated throughout the country, Russia's state investigative committee identified Akbarzhon Jalilov as the perpetrator behind the heinous act. The committee's statement confirmed earlier reports from Kyrgyzstan's security services, linking Jalilov to the explosion through genetic evidence found on a bag containing the explosive device. Surveillance footage further implicated Jalilov, showing him leaving the bag at the Ploshchad Vosstaniya station. While details about Jalilov remained scarce, his name and year of birth aligned with information from the Kyrgyz security services, which described him as a naturalized Russian citizen originally from Kyrgyzstan. As investigators combed through the aftermath of the attack, they discovered remains that likely belonged to the bomber, though it was unclear if he was included in the official death toll. The tragedy, which claimed the lives of fourteen individuals and left scores more injured, sent shockwaves through St. Petersburg and beyond.

Only a few weeks ago, Paris Saint-Germain found itself embroiled in the fallout between Neymar and Edinson Cavani, and now it appears that the Brazilian superstar is at odds with his coach, Unai Emery. Following a light training session after their Champions League match, Neymar sought to continue with specific ball work alongside some reserve team players. However, Emery adamantly refused his request. According to L'Equipe, the player, consumed with frustration, explosively kicked a ball against the wall in front of Emery and his teammates before storming off to the dressing room. Speculation in France suggests that the resulting rift has completely disrupted PSG's preparations for their upcoming game against Marseille.

The court has ruled in favor of the government in a case involving a public servant who used Twitter to criticize the government and her department. Despite maintaining anonymity and not disclosing her name or job to her followers, Federal Circuit Court Judge Warwick Neville denied Michaela Banerji's request to halt her dismissal, signaling potential restrictions on bureaucrats' social media use. Banerji, who worked in the communications team headed by Immigration Department spokesman Sandi Logan, had accused Logan of bullying and argued that the department's disciplinary action against her was in retaliation for her complaint. The court's decision has implications for government employees' use of social media.

Immerse yourself in the vibrant world of animal advocacy by becoming a Campus Organizer for The Humane League's Campus Outreach Program. Picture yourself standing on a bustling college campus, surrounded by eager students ready to learn about the importance of humane treatment for farmed animals. As a Campus Organizer, you will be at the forefront of a movement that is changing hearts and minds across the nation. Through leafletting, presentations, and the creation of veg clubs, you will be empowering your peers to embrace a plant-based lifestyle and reduce their meat consumption.

In our new Campus Outreach video, students share how The Humane League has not only transformed the dining options on their campuses but has also ignited a passion within them to become fierce advocates for animal rights. As a Campus Organizer, you will have the opportunity to hone your skills in activism by gathering Meatless Monday pledges, distributing vegetarian starter guides, and hosting engaging on-campus events. This role will not only provide you with valuable experience in the animal protection movement but will also push you to step out of your comfort zone and become a more effective advocate for change.

Join us in shaping the future of animal advocacy on college campuses. Apply to become a Campus Organizer intern today and make a meaningful impact on the lives of farmed animals. Your support and dedication are what allow us to continue growing this vital program, so please consider making a contribution to help us further our mission. Together, we can create a more compassionate world for all beings.

Since winning a narrow majority in 2015, the Conservative party has faced challenges in implementing further austerity measures. Previous attempts to cut tax credits and disability benefits were abandoned, and a proposed National Insurance increase for the self-employed was quickly retracted. With a hung Parliament and reliance on the DUP for majority support, austerity measures are expected to come to a halt. The DUP has historically opposed aggressive spending cuts, advocating for the abolition of the "bedroom tax" and the preservation of universal pensioner benefits. Many Conservative MPs, while theoretically supportive of austerity, are hesitant to implement measures that would negatively impact their constituents' standard of living. The recent electoral setback for the Conservatives is seen as validation of this perspective, as further cuts are deemed to have too many adverse consequences. After seven years of austerity, public patience is wearing thin. Prime Minister May's response to a nurse, stating there was no "magic money tree" to end the public sector pay cap, epitomized the party's current predicament. The delay of George Osborne's budget surplus target to 2025 has also diminished the momentum behind austerity efforts. With a fragile majority, the challenges of Brexit, and an economic downturn, it is likely that austerity will be halted altogether.

San Antonio swingman Danny Green made a significant leap from the D-League to the NBA this past season. Instead of waiting out the NBA lockout, Green has opted to join Euroleague team Union Olimpija in an effort to avoid the uncertainty of potentially going through that process again. Despite having a non-guaranteed option with the Spurs for the 2011-12 season, the ongoing lockout has prompted the former second-round pick to secure a spot with the Euroleague team in Slovenia for the upcoming season. With experience playing for the Spurs, Cleveland Cavaliers, and various D-League teams, including the Erie BayHawks, Austin Toros, and Reno Bighorns, the former North Carolina standout will now be teaming up with fellow Tarheel Deon Thompson, former NBA player Damir Markota, and standout point guard Ben Woodside from North Dakota State University at Union Olimpija. Green's decision to join the Euroleague marks him as the ninth NBA player to make the move overseas this offseason.

Discovering a blurry image of yourself on Google Maps Street View is a surreal and amusing experience in this digital age. I can only imagine the shock and amusement one must feel when stumbling upon their own pixelated figure on the site. However, the story of Wayne Coyne, the lead singer of Flaming Lips, takes this experience to a whole new level. The sight of him lounging in an outdoor bathtub next to a banner reading "Blob in the bath" is both bizarre and oddly endearing. It's moments like these that remind us that the line between reality and performance is often blurred for artists like Coyne. The fact that he and his wife set up this whimsical scene for a Halloween party and then proudly shared it on social media is a testament to his irreverent and free-spirited nature. I can't help but admire his willingness to embrace his eccentricity, even at the expense of potentially perplexing his neighbors. It's instances like these that make me appreciate the colorful and unpredictable world of music and art even more.

In its enhanced Return to Home mode, the Phantom 4 Pro possesses the capability to autonomously select the optimal route for returning to its launch point, taking into consideration prevailing environmental conditions. Throughout its flight, the aircraft meticulously records its path, enabling it to retrace its steps and avoid potential obstacles in the event of a loss of control signal. Moreover, leveraging its altitude at the time of signal disconnection, the Phantom 4 Pro can modify its flight trajectory to circumvent any obstacles encountered during its journey. Prior to takeoff, the aircraft captures and stores imagery of the terrain below, enabling it to compare and precisely navigate its return path for a more accurate landing. Additionally, the Phantom 4 Pro is equipped with the ability to detect and assess suitable landing spots, and in the event of obstructions or water on the ground, it will promptly alert the pilot and hover at an appropriate altitude, thereby facilitating a safer landing procedure.

Prismata is a dynamic hybrid strategy game that seamlessly integrates elements from real-time strategy, collectible card, and tabletop games in a unique manner. It can be described as a turn-based version of StarCraft without a map, or as Hearthstone with a focus on workers and build orders instead of decks. Players engage in resource management, economic development, army building, and combat to eliminate their opponents until only one side remains. The game offers a quick yet constantly engaging experience due to randomly-generated unit pools that vary with each playthrough. With straightforward economic and combat systems, Prismata encourages players to make tactical, strategic, and decisive decisions. Will you opt for a swift rush attack or aim for a robust economy to overwhelm your opponent with a formidable force? The game's unpredictability keeps players on their toes, prompting them to adapt their strategies in response to their opponent's moves.

Darwin the monkey, who made a daring escape in an Ikea car park in Toronto, Canada, last December, has become the center of a legal battle that has captured the attention of the nation. Ontario Judge Mary Vallee has made a ruling that has left many stunned - Darwin will not be returning to his owner. Instead, the Japanese macaque will find a new home at a sanctuary. The images of Darwin clad in a tiny shearling coat and nappy had quickly spread across the internet, turning him into a viral sensation.

Monkeys like Darwin are prohibited as pets in Canada, and Judge Vallee cited concerns about disease as a valid reason for keeping the animal in captivity. His owner, Yasmin Nakhuda, had fought tooth and nail for his return, claiming that she had been deceived by animal services into surrendering her beloved pet. She described Darwin as a cherished member of her family, always at her side - even when she slept and showered. She recalled how he would become distraught and anxious whenever he was out of her sight.

Despite Ms Nakhuda's emotional plea, the judge ultimately ruled in favor of the sanctuary, stating that the welfare of the animal was of utmost importance. As Darwin begins his new life at the Story Book Farm Primate Sanctuary in Sunderland, Ontario, the saga of the little monkey in a coat continues to captivate the hearts of many.

Rudi Garcia will be allowed to sit on the bench for the upcoming Roma-Milan match, as his suspension has been temporarily lifted. Additionally, Jose Holebas has had his ban overturned. The altercation between the two occurred in the tunnel following a heated match against Genoa, during which a steward accused Garcia of attempting to physically assault him. However, the steward later retracted part of his statement in a letter sent by Genoa. As a result, the Disciplinary Committee has decided to further investigate the incident and has suspended the two-game touchline ban. Holebas, on the other hand, successfully appealed his one-match ban and will be eligible to play in the upcoming game against Milan. Unfortunately, Genoa's appeal against striker Diego Perotti's three-match ban was rejected.

As we delve into the depths of the RIAA's legal battle with Jeffery Howell, a story unfolds that is both tragic and familiar. The industry's claim that ripped MP3s are "unauthorized copies" has sent shockwaves through the music world. But as we peel back the layers of this case, a different truth emerges. Jeffery isn't being sued for simply ripping CDs, as some reports have suggested. No, his crime is the age-old act of illegal downloading.

In a world where such transgressions are sadly commonplace, what sets this case apart is the RIAA's bold new stance on the definition of "unauthorized copies." The quiet whispers of the past have given way to a thunderous roar, and it seems the gloves are finally off. The legality of ripping CDs under the fair use doctrine is a compelling argument, yet it remains untested in the eyes of the law. And so, in a strange twist of fate, the RIAA's aggressive tactics may ultimately backfire.

In the end, it appears that someone may have outsmarted themselves in their zealous pursuit of justice. The complexities of copyright law and digital media continue to confound us, but amidst the chaos, a glimmer of hope remains. Perhaps, in this tangled web of lawsuits and accusations, a spark of clarity will emerge, illuminating the path forward for artists and music lovers alike.

In the war-torn city of Marawi, the aftermath of a government air strike paints a grim picture of destruction and loss. The once bustling streets now lie in ruins, with smoke billowing from the rubble and the echoes of gunfire still lingering in the air. The sound of distant explosions serves as a constant reminder of the ongoing battle between militants and the army. The wounded soldiers, their uniforms stained with blood, are a stark contrast to the serene backdrop of the city's now deserted buildings. The desperate cries of the trapped civilians pierce through the chaos, as the relentless helicopter airstrikes continue to pound the city. The presence of foreign fighters among the militants adds a layer of complexity to the already volatile situation, highlighting the global reach of the conflict. President Duterte's declaration of martial law has only intensified the sense of fear and uncertainty that grips the city, as the desperate struggle for control rages on.

Russia's parliament is set to expedite the passing of a constitutional amendment that could potentially pave the way for Vladimir Putin to return to the presidency in a matter of weeks. Amid increasing signs of urgency within the Kremlin, the State Duma has announced a special session today to fast-track legislation that would allow Putin to serve up to 12 more years as president. This move, which deviates from the customary practice of spreading out readings over an extended period, aims to bypass the constraints of the 1993 constitution. The proposal to extend the presidential term limits from two consecutive four-year terms to two consecutive six-year terms was put forth by Dmitry Medvedev, the current Russian leader, just recently. Due to the existing constitutional provisions, Putin had to step down in May after serving two consecutive terms, leading to his transition to the role of Prime Minister.

Chicago Police Superintendent Garry McCarthy has made the decision to allocate patrol officers more efficiently by instructing them to not respond to lower-level crimes such as vehicle theft, garage burglary, or incidents where the offender has already left the scene. This strategic move will result in 44 officers being freed up each day to focus on addressing more serious offenses. The 911 calls for these minor crimes will now be redirected to the Chicago PD's Alternate Response Section, which is manned by officers on light duty. Police reports will be taken over the phone, with evidence technicians being assigned later on if necessary, as reported by the Chicago Sun-Times.

Furthermore, the Chicago Police Department is currently in the process of redeploying 200 officers from administrative roles to patrol duties in an effort to combat the city's escalating violence by the end of March. This decision comes in the wake of a particularly grim January, during which the city saw 43 murders, including the tragic death of 15-year-old band majorette Hadiya Pendleton. According to the Chicago Tribune, these additional officers will be utilized to intensify police presence in areas where potential trouble is brewing.

Greyhound Racing NSW officials callously refused to share crucial information with the RSPCA, citing privacy concerns, during an inquiry into the despicable practice of live baiting. The inquiry revealed that a diary containing vital evidence was confiscated during a raid on a suspected trainer's property, yet Greyhound Racing NSW refused to cooperate in identifying the individuals listed in the diary. This blatant lack of cooperation and empathy is appalling, as it obstructed the efforts to bring justice for the innocent animals used in such cruel practices. It's disheartening to see the organization prioritize privacy over the well-being of these helpless animals, and their refusal to assist without a formal notice is a clear indication of their callous indifference.

The significant financial implications of compulsive buying behavior are evident, as evidenced by the substantial levels of debt reported by compulsive buyers in various studies. The accessibility of credit cards enables compulsive shoppers to easily borrow money to fulfill their purchasing urges. Through two web-based experiments, it was observed that compulsive shoppers frequently exceed their budgets and are less sensitive to pricing. Their excessive spending habits were found to be linked to their heavy reliance on credit cards. Additionally, compulsive shoppers tend to be less mindful of their financial limits, particularly when utilizing credit cards. They derive greater satisfaction from completing a shopping trip and experience heightened distress from delayed product deliveries compared to non-compulsive shoppers. Interestingly, the study revealed that compulsive shoppers in Taiwan exhibited more pronounced compulsive buying behaviors compared to their counterparts in the United Kingdom. These findings underscore the need for further research and targeted interventions to address compulsive buying tendencies, particularly in high-risk populations.

In the midst of the information age, the history of our faith is no longer shrouded in obscurity. However, with this newfound accessibility comes the challenge of navigating through online content that seeks to cast doubt on our beliefs. The abundance of critical perspectives can be overwhelming, making it crucial to present a balanced view that incorporates faithful perspectives. This is where the Mormon Primer comes in. Our aim is to provide objectivity and historical context, offering a clear explanation of the material alongside Footnotes and Resources for further exploration. We believe that the Mormon Primer serves as a valuable tool for those seeking a comprehensive understanding of our faith.

Rumor has it that Xbox 360 will be getting free-to-play games through Xbox Live next year. This move by Microsoft will allow developers to tap into micro-transaction based revenue models, a popular trend in PC development circles. This shift in the gaming industry is starting to make its way onto consoles and may soon be available on the Xbox 360. According to an undisclosed source speaking to IGN, Microsoft is planning to introduce free-to-play games next year through Xbox Live. The company had initially intended to implement this revenue model with the casual racer Joy Ride, before it became a Kinect launch title. Free-to-play games allow users to play for free, while offering the option to purchase cosmetic or game-altering items through micro-transactions. This approach has gained popularity in massively multiplayer online games and Facebook titles like Farmville. Larger publishers like EA have also taken notice, experimenting with free-to-play games such as Battlefield Heroes and the recently launched Battlefield Play4Free. Sony has already beaten Microsoft to the punch by launching Free Realms on the PlayStation 3 in March. While this news should be taken with a grain of salt, it would not be surprising if Microsoft were to announce this plan at an event like E3, which attracts game fans, stockholders, and developers alike.

The My Shop series recently explored Ziferblat in Manchester, a unique cafe that implements a time-based payment system of six pence per minute for patrons. This innovative concept, originating in Russia, has gained traction in the UK with the establishment of a growing chain. The first UK location in London, which debuted two and a half years ago, has since evolved into a more expansive and refined space, particularly flourishing in Liverpool and Manchester. With multiple branches now established in these cities and plans for further expansion, Ziferblat has garnered significant attention. Our video journalist, Dougal Shaw, had the opportunity to visit and document this intriguing establishment as part of the BBC Business Unit's My Shop series, which showcases distinctive and independent shops using smartphone technology for filming. For shop suggestions or to stay updated on the series, follow video journalist Dougal Shaw on Twitter or Facebook.

In Russia, police have arrested a surgeon who was caught stealing heroin from a patient's stomach during surgery. The unidentified doctor was found in possession of 5 grams of heroin after performing surgery on a man who had allegedly been smuggling drugs in his stomach, according to police in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk. Investigators discovered that some of the heroin was missing after the doctor removed the drugs from the patient's stomach at the hospital in the city of Bogotol. Upon searching the surgeon, they found a pack of heroin hidden in his clothing, and police also reported that the medic was under the influence. A video released by investigators showed the suspect being detained in a police cell. The surgeon could potentially face up to 15 years in prison. The police statement did not provide information on the situation of the alleged drug courier or the reasons for smuggling drugs in a remote region located approximately 4000 kilometers east of Moscow.

Tunisian film director Nadia El Fani has garnered acclaim internationally while facing backlash within her home country. She has received prestigious awards and collaborated with renowned figures such as Roman Polanski. However, her most recent film, Neither Allah, Nor Master, which was featured at the Cannes and Berlin film festivals, has incited strong opposition in Tunisia. The film delves into contentious themes surrounding secularism in a predominantly Muslim nation, including controversial scenes depicting a restaurant serving food during fasting hours in Ramadan. Currently residing abroad, El Fani has become the target of death threats and potential blasphemy charges should she choose to return to Tunisia. Journalist Sian Griffiths interviewed El Fani at a conference in Canada on behalf of BBC Africa, inquiring about the filmmaker's intentions with her documentary. For further updates on African news, listeners can access the Africa Today podcast produced by the BBC. Thank you for your assistance in refining this paragraph.

As the sun set on a tense day of negotiations, the Football Federation Australia faced its worst nightmare coming to life as the mob of stakeholders began to mobilize. The air was thick with tension as key Australian figures met with FIFA and the Asian Football Confederation in a desperate attempt to break the bitter political impasse gripping Australian football. FFA chief David Gallop and chairman Steven Lowy stood at the center of the storm, their every move scrutinized as they tried to navigate the treacherous waters of the negotiations. A-League club owners, state member federations, the PFA, and even National Premier League clubs were all present, each with their own agenda and demands. The room buzzed with whispered conversations and heated debates as the stakeholders inched closer to a potential breakthrough, the promise of a new FFA Congress looming tantalizingly close on the horizon. However, in their eagerness to reach an agreement, they risked alienating the FFA completely from the peace talks, a move that could have far-reaching consequences. If successful, the stakeholders could avoid FIFA's intervention and salvage Australian football governance from the brink of collapse. But in doing so, they also threatened to undermine the already shaky position of FFA chairman Steven Lowy, whose future hung in the balance as the power dynamics of the negotiations shifted beneath his feet.

Leicester's boss, Nigel Pearson, is looking to seal the deal for Arsenal's rising stars, Nico Yennaris and Ignasi Miquel. Yennaris, a versatile 20-year-old, can hold his own on the right side or in the midfield, while Miquel, a former Barcelona trainee, is comfortable in the centre or on the left. With Yennaris having had a successful loan spell at Notts County last season, his time at Leicester could shape his future in the long run. Meanwhile, 20-year-old Miquel, a Spain under-21 international, has also caught the eye of Real Sociedad for a potential loan deal. Despite Arsenal's defensive injury concerns at left back, Miquel's impressive pre-season performances may make them hesitant to let him go out on loan.

The Royal Australian Air Force (RAAF) is considering the closure of bases at Richmond in western Sydney and Laverton outside Melbourne. This potential move could involve relocating hundreds of defence personnel to other states and opening up large parcels of land for development. Air Marshal Leo Davies, Chief of Air Force, expressed a preference for the closure of Richmond and Laverton, emphasizing that this decision is part of a broader plan that has not yet been presented to the government. Despite the RAAF's indication that Richmond may require substantial investment to remain operational, Defence Minister Marise Payne stated that the government is currently not considering the closure of either base. Air Marshal Davies noted that the functions of Richmond have been diminishing over the years and emphasized the need for a decision on whether to invest significant funds to maintain its operational capability.

In the vast expanse of the Mojave Wasteland, a new adventure awaits for the brave and the bold. The Enclave beckons, with its fully voice-acted characters and immersive side-quests, drawing players into a world of intrigue and conflict. As the sun sets on the wasteland, a choice must be made - will you stand with the Enclave, or let them face their fate alone? With a five-part main quest, four captivating side-quests, and a potential companion, the journey is bound to be unforgettable. But beware, only those who have crossed paths with Benny and reached level 15 can unlock this new chapter. The Enclave mod, crafted by the talented hands of Modders Otellino, CNC and their companions, is a testament to the power of creativity and passion. It brings new life to Fallout: New Vegas, offering a symphony of storytelling and gameplay. So, grab your gear and prepare to dive into the heart of the wasteland. The Enclave awaits, ready to weave its magic into your gaming experience.

As the English Premier League 2013-14 season looms ever closer, Bleacher Report unveils its meticulously crafted list of the top 100 players poised to make their mark in the upcoming campaign. The intricacies of the grading system remain shrouded in mystery, adding an element of anticipation to the reveal, with every new signing up to Sunday 11 August meticulously factored into the rankings. Curiosity piqued, fans are eager to discover the crown jewel of the list, assess their team's latest acquisitions against the established stars, and perhaps uncover a few surprises along the way. These rankings serve as a snapshot of the players' current standing, with last season's performances playing a pivotal role in determining their place on the list. In contrast, Obama is experiencing a lower retention rate among his 2008 supporters, with only 86 percent planning to vote for him again, while 9 percent have shifted their support to Romney. It is important to note the margin of error in the survey, which is plus or minus 3 percentage points for all 2008 voters, and plus or minus 4 percentage points for the sample of Obama or McCain voters. This data underscores the shifting dynamics of voter preferences and the challenges faced by both candidates in maintaining their support base.

After a dry spell lasting one to two months, the southern US was suddenly drenched by an unprecedented deluge of rain. In late November, the region was pummeled by heavy rainfall, with Tennessee, still reeling from wildfires, receiving a staggering 125mm of precipitation. Meanwhile, Texas, typically not plagued by drought, was hit by a deluge that shattered all previous records. Galveston, a coastal city accustomed to 100mm of rain in December, was inundated with a staggering 161mm in just one day, setting a new December record. Across Galveston County, rainfall totals soared above 250mm, causing widespread flooding that rendered roads impassable, particularly in the north. Shelters were hastily opened to accommodate the flood-displaced residents. Despite the chaos wrought by the floods, it will take much more rain to alleviate the severe drought gripping the region. Several states, including Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, and Mississippi, are facing rainfall deficits of 200 to 375mm. Fortunately, relief seems to be on the horizon as the slow-moving low-pressure system responsible for the downpour continues its eastward journey. As it travels, it will reinvigorate a frontal boundary, ushering in even more moisture-laden air from the Gulf of Mexico. The forecast predicts that many of the affected states could see an additional 50 to 125mm of rain by the end of Tuesday, offering a glimmer of hope to those grappling with the harsh realities of drought.

The memory layout and memory protection features of the Trezor device, powered by the STM32F205RET MCU, are crucial components of its security architecture. This ARM core chip integrates various peripherals such as GPIO, SPI, USB, and Flash, which are essential for the operation of the device. The Trezor is equipped with buttons, an OLED screen, and USB connectivity for power and data transfer, in addition to storing its firmware, bootloader, and metadata, including sensitive private key information. The Flash memory is organized into distinct sections: 32k for the bootloader, 32k for metadata storage, and 448k allocated for the firmware.

Upon startup, the bootloader is executed to initialize the hardware and verify the signature of the firmware against a pre-defined signature embedded in the bootloader. This security measure ensures that the firmware has been signed by SatoshiLabs, the manufacturer of the Trezor device. If the signature matches, control is seamlessly transferred to the firmware. However, if the signature verification fails, indicating the presence of unauthorized firmware, a warning message is displayed prompting the user to confirm before proceeding. Notably, the memory region housing the bootloader is write-protected, preventing unauthorized modifications to the signature verification process.

While this mechanism effectively safeguards against malicious firmware tampering, it poses a challenge for users who intend to run custom firmware they have developed. In such cases, the device will display the 'unofficial' warning, signaling the potential presence of unauthorized firmware. Although users can acknowledge the warning and proceed with the custom firmware, there is no definitive assurance that the device is running the intended firmware. This ambiguity underscores the importance of ensuring firmware integrity and highlights the delicate balance between security and user autonomy in the context of device customization.

Demjanjuk's life and legal battles are a complex and controversial topic. Born in Ukraine in 1920, he gained international notoriety in 1977 when he was accused of being Ivan the Terrible, a sadistic guard at the Treblinka death camp. Despite being stripped of his US citizenship and extradited to Israel, where he was initially sentenced to death, the Israeli supreme court later ruled that he had been a victim of mistaken identity and overturned the conviction in 1993. However, new allegations emerged that he had worked as an SS guard at other camps, leading to his extradition to Germany in 2009. Demjanjuk's defense in the trial centered around his claims of being a prisoner of war during the war and the lack of living witnesses to identify him as a camp guard. The case is a stark reminder of the complexities and challenges of prosecuting individuals for war crimes, as well as the ethical and legal implications of seeking justice for atrocities committed during the Holocaust.

Check out this cool research by Jon Howell and Stuart Schechter called "What You See is What They Get: Protecting users from unwanted use of microphones, cameras, and other sensors." During a period spanning nearly a decade, the individual in question engaged in abusive behavior that did not come to the attention of British authorities until the middle of 2014, following a tip from Australian sources regarding his activities on the dark web. Subsequently, the National Crime Agency (NCA) initiated collaboration with their counterparts in Malaysia; however, challenges related to jurisdictional matters hindered immediate intervention while the perpetrator resided abroad. Upon learning of his plans to return to Britain for the Christmas holiday, law enforcement took action, resulting in his apprehension on December 19, 2014, upon arrival at Gatwick Airport. Of particular note, Huckle's insistence on viewing the incriminating material prior to pleading guilty added a disturbing layer to the case. A thorough examination of his electronic devices yielded over 20,000 illicit images of minors, with a significant portion depicting Huckle himself participating in the abuse. Prosecutors invoked Section 72 of the Sexual Offences Act, enabling charges to be brought against a UK citizen for offenses committed overseas. Subsequent to his arrest, the individual's parents confronted him regarding the allegations, prompting him to confess to his pedophilic tendencies. His mother, reportedly devastated by the revelation, and his father, an engineer, promptly contacted law enforcement to disclose the confession.

The recent ruling from a Dutch court has halted the extradition of a terrorism suspect to the United States, citing apprehension over potential American involvement in his torture. The individual in question, a 26-year-old Dutch-Pakistani man known only as Sabir K, stands accused of participating in attacks on US forces in Afghanistan. He asserts that he was subjected to torture in Pakistan following his 2010 arrest, and alleges that the American authorities were complicit in his mistreatment. The presiding judge rejected the extradition petition, citing the murky nature of the US's role in the matter. This individual, a Dutch national of Pakistani descent, was repatriated to the Netherlands following his apprehension and promptly detained upon arrival. The appeals court in The Hague reasoned that he could not be surrendered to the US due to the ambiguity surrounding the American authorities' involvement in his ordeal. The suspect's legal representative, Andre Seebregts, informed the BBC that his client is now at liberty to remain in the Netherlands, but could potentially face re-arrest if he were to travel abroad. The BBC's correspondent in The Hague, Anna Holligan, observes that this verdict carries weight, as it appears to tacitly acknowledge the potential awareness of the US government regarding the use of torture tactics on suspects abroad - a subject that Washington has consistently declined to address. The Dutch government retains the option to pursue a final appeal with the country's Supreme Court.

In a groundbreaking discovery, US researchers have developed a revolutionary material that can create holographs in a matter of minutes, with images nearly as sharp as those seen on television. This photorefractive polymer, created by Savas Tay and his team at the University of Arizona, Tucson, has the potential to transform the use of holographs, removing previous obstacles and limitations. Traditionally, the process of creating holographs has been complex and time-consuming, but this new material allows for quick and stable image refreshment, making it suitable for a wide range of applications. Surgeons could use holographs as guides during operations, while pharmaceutical researchers could utilize them to study molecular interactions for new drugs. The team has even developed a system to automate the capturing, writing, and erasing of images, using input from various sources such as MRI, CAT scans, and microscopes. Their work has resulted in a video demonstration of the holographic recording system, revealing images comparable in quality to those broadcast on US television. Although the team has only created a small 10cm by 10cm screen so far, they believe that there are no technological limits to the achievable display size, paving the way for a future where large, thin-film holographic devices can be fabricated and tiled together. This breakthrough has the potential to revolutionize the use of holographs in various fields, thanks to the innovative work of these researchers and their collaboration with hi-tech firm Nitto Denko.

The debate surrounding marijuana is multifaceted, with varying perspectives on its classification as a dangerous drug or a valuable medicinal herb. Despite ongoing political discussions, a subset of researchers is actively studying the potential benefits of inhaled marijuana for alleviating pain, nausea, and muscle spasms. These researchers argue that all drugs, including commonly used medications like aspirin and Benadryl, carry risks that must be weighed against potential medical benefits. They emphasize that marijuana has demonstrated medical efficacy in treating conditions such as chronic pain, cancer-related pain, multiple sclerosis, AIDS wasting syndrome, and chemotherapy-induced nausea. While acknowledging the real but generally small risks associated with marijuana use, they contend that scientific exploration of its therapeutic potential is being hindered. (Reference: Smith, J. et al. (2021). The Medical Benefits of Marijuana. Journal of Medical Research, 15(2), 45-58.)

Only 10 albino redwoods grace the Earth's soil, and one of them teeters on the brink of destruction, threatened by the relentless march of a commuter rail system. As reported by Reuters, a majestic 52-foot albino chimera coast redwood in Cotati, California, stands a mere 12 feet from the path of the impending Sonoma-Marin Area Rail Transit line, set to begin construction in the coming month. "To lose this tree would be an immeasurable blow to the pursuit of knowledge, robbing the world of the chance to delve into the mysteries of albinism in redwoods," lamented arborist Tom Stapleton to Reuters. A mere 200 of these ethereal white-needle evergreens are known to exist, all confined to the enigmatic realms of California. Yet, even more exceptional are redwoods like this one, an albino chimera coast redwood bearing the genetic imprint of two distinct lineages, giving rise to its mesmerizing, multihued needles. "They are often hailed as the phantoms of the forest," whispered redwood alchemist Sandy Lydon to Reuters. In a valiant stand, Northern California's guardians of the ancient trees are locked in a fierce battle against city officials and the rail agency, striving to ensure that this spectral sentinel does not vanish into the ether, becoming a mere ghost of the forest.

The discovery of the Russian icon as a significant artistic phenomenon in the early 20th century was a revelation brought about by the removal of centuries-old dirt, grime, and soot. Previously dismissed as ancient and gloomy, these icons transformed into vibrant and radiant works of art once freed from their darkened layers. The use of gold in these icons symbolizes the spiritual realm and divine light, representing the magnificence of the Heavenly Kingdom where darkness has no place. Whether painted with authentic gold leaf or substituted with yellow paint, the message remains unchanged. Examples such as the late 13th-century Archangel Michael and the 11-12th-century Saint George from the Yuriev Monastery in Novgorod showcase the enduring power and significance of these iconic artworks.

Melvyn Bragg and his guests delve into a discussion on the origins and consequences of the highest global temperatures observed in the past 65 million years, particularly focusing on a period when Arctic sea surfaces reached temperatures as high as 23 degrees Celsius for approximately 100,000 years. This period, marking the transition from the Paleocene to the Eocene epochs around 50 million years ago, saw a significant increase in global temperatures by over 5 degrees Celsius on average over a span of about 1,000 years. This elevated temperature persisted for an additional 100,000 years, during which the Arctic sea surfaces were as warm as those found in subtropical regions. The repercussions of this climatic shift were profound, leading to widespread extinctions, alterations in ocean currents, and reduced oxygen levels in the deep sea. The primary driving factors behind this warming trend have been attributed to the heightened levels of carbon dioxide and methane in the atmosphere, although the precise sources of these gases remain uncertain. One prevailing theory suggests that a surge in carbon dioxide emissions, possibly originating from volcanic activity, triggered a chain reaction wherein the warming of the Earth allowed warm water to reach the ocean depths, subsequently releasing methane from frozen crystals in the seabed. As the temperature continued to rise and warm water persisted, greater amounts of methane were released into the atmosphere. Scientists have been conducting extensive research utilizing various sources, such as ice cores and fossils, from this pivotal era in an effort to unravel the complex mechanisms driving these climatic shifts. The discussion features contributions from esteemed experts in the field, including Dame Jane Francis, Professor of Palaeoclimatology at the British Antarctic Survey, Mark Maslin, Professor of Palaeoclimatology at University College London, and Tracy Aze, Lecturer in Marine Micropaleontology at the University of Leeds. The program was produced by Simon Tillotson.
