We decided to elevate the classic BLT with a generous dollop of Baconnaise, and as I carefully spread it onto the toasted bread, I couldn't help but feel a surge of anticipation. As we took our first bites, I found myself caught in a whirlwind of conflicting emotions - from the desire to grab a spoon and indulge in the rich, smoky flavor, to the nagging thought that maybe I still preferred good old BBQ sauce. Denine, on the other hand, found solace in the subtle, balanced bacon flavor, and we both agreed that the addition of actual bacon bits would take the experience to the next level. As we contemplate our next move, our precious jar of Baconnaise sits proudly on the top shelf of the fridge, awaiting further exploration. The Baconnaise fever has officially made its mark in our city, and I am eager to see where this flavorful journey takes us next.

The latest installment of the renowned Japanese hack-and-slash franchise, Dynasty Warriors 9, has recently been unveiled by publisher Koei Tecmo. Marking a significant departure from its predecessors, this ninth iteration will embrace an open-world format for the first time in the series' history. A teaser trailer in Japanese has been made available for preview, showcasing the forthcoming title. Despite the numerical discrepancy on the title screen, it should be noted that the numbering of Dynasty Warriors titles in Japan lags behind their western counterparts. Notably, producer Akihiro Suzuki has characterized Dynasty Warriors 9 as a "rebirth" of the franchise, with developer Omega Force undertaking the ambitious task of encapsulating the entirety of China within a single in-game map. The forthcoming game is set to feature the return of all 83 playable characters from Dynasty Warriors 8, alongside a roster of new combatants, such as Zhou Cang, a figure inspired by the classic literary work "Romance of the Three Kingdoms." Following an earlier announcement from Koei Tecmo in January concerning a major revelation related to Dynasty Warriors, anticipation has been mounting for this latest release, especially considering that the previous core installment, Dynasty Warriors 8, was released back in 2013. In the interim, fans have been able to enjoy expansions to the game as well as a Zelda-themed spinoff, Hyrule Warriors, for the Wii U and 3DS platforms. While specific details regarding the release date and compatible platforms for Dynasty Warriors 9 remain scarce at present, GameSpot is committed to providing timely updates as soon as new information becomes available.

One of the department's reasons for not disclosing the aerial surveillance program was its existing use of security cameras in Compton city parks and at the Gateway Town Center. However, this justification falls short for a program of such vast scope. While it is possible that both citizens and officials would have agreed that enhanced security justified a camera-equipped Cessna flying over the entire city to capture images of residents' backyard activities, there are signs that the Sheriff's Department was aware that this would not sit well with the public. A department official involved in the project admitted to the Center for Investigative Reporting that the program was kept confidential to avoid potential complaints, acknowledging that many people have concerns about intrusive surveillance practices.

Immerse yourself in a world of endless possibilities with Social Fixer, a tool designed to enhance your Facebook experience. Customize your news feed by filtering posts based on content, author, and more, allowing you to curate a feed that resonates with your interests. Say goodbye to unwanted Sponsored Posts, political rants, and other distractions that clutter your feed. With the ability to hide posts you've already read and customize the interface to your liking, Social Fixer empowers you to take control of your social media experience. Dive deeper into conversations with the Comment Navigator feature, highlighting older comments and expanding replies for a more engaging interaction. Transform your browsing experience with Stealth Mode, allowing you to browse Facebook incognito without accidentally engaging with posts. Stay up to date with regular updates and new features that aim to elevate your Facebook experience to new heights. Let Social Fixer be your guide as you navigate the ever-changing landscape of social media.

The legal action taken by Jennifer Chong, the Australian widow of a passenger who died on Malaysia Airlines flight MH370, is a poignant reminder of the devastating impact of the tragedy on the families left behind. By suing the airline for compensation, Mrs Chong is seeking justice and accountability for the loss of her husband, Chong Ling Tan. The fact that her husband was seated in business class on the ill-fated flight highlights the severity of the situation and the potential negligence on the part of Malaysia Airlines. The official declaration by the Malaysian Department of Civil Aviation that the disappearance of the plane was an accident with no survivors further underscores the need for Malaysia Airlines to take responsibility for the consequences of this tragedy. Mrs Chong's legal action is not just about seeking financial compensation, but also about demanding transparency, accountability, and closure for the families affected by the disappearance of flight MH370.

It is with a heavy heart that we must convey the unfortunate news of Muse's upcoming performances in Oslo, Stockholm, and Malmo being cancelled due to the grievous injury sustained by Matt, who has fractured two bones in his foot. The band, in their unwavering commitment to delivering a stellar live experience, have arrived at the poignant decision to forgo these shows, recognizing that Matt's performance on crutches would not do justice to their artistry nor the devoted fans who have eagerly purchased tickets. Muse humbly extends their sincerest apologies to all those affected by this unforeseen turn of events. Refunds for the cancelled shows can be obtained from the original point of sale. While Matt's recovery is diligently monitored in the days ahead, the remaining tour dates remain steadfastly on the calendar. Any updates on his condition will be promptly disseminated through the Muse website, as well as their official social media channels.

The daughter of a former US congressman, Katrina Lantos Swett, whose father survived the horrors of the Holocaust, has taken a bold stand by returning a prestigious award to Hungary in defiance of its decision to honor a writer accused of anti-Semitism. Bestowed with the Knight's Cross of the Order of Merit for her tireless efforts in advocating for minority rights, Swett expressed profound dismay at the country's decision to also bestow the same award upon Zsolt Bayer, whose controversial writings have been deemed as abhorrent. She declared that the sanctity of the Knight's Cross had been tarnished by the association with Bayer, asserting that he merited condemnation rather than accolades for his abhorrent rhetoric. Swett joins a growing chorus of dissent, with approximately 100 other recipients of Hungarian state awards returning them in protest against the decision to honor Bayer. In a resolute act of defiance, Swett hopes to compel the Hungarian government to reconsider its endorsement of the inflammatory writer, who has propagated hateful narratives targeting marginalized communities, including comparing the Roma population to animals and casting aspersions on Muslims. Swett, recognized for her outstanding contributions in establishing the Tom Lantos Institute in Budapest, a bastion for championing minority rights, has underscored the imperative for moral rectitude in such matters. The US Holocaust Memorial Museum has urged Hungary's leadership to rescind the award conferred upon Bayer, emphasizing the gravity of the situation. While Bayer has sought to amend his past transgressions by expressing regret for his inflammatory language, the reverberations of his incendiary rhetoric continue to resonate, calling into question the integrity of the accolade bestowed upon him for his purportedly "exemplary journalistic activities". As the saga unfolds, Swett's unwavering defiance stands as a testament to the enduring battle against bigotry and intolerance, transcending borders and ideologies in the pursuit of justice and dignity for all.

The meeting between United Nations Syria envoy Staffan de Mistura and Russian defence minister Sergei Shoigu in Moscow on Wednesday marked a crucial step towards ending the six-year war in Syria. Their discussions focused on transitioning from de-escalation zones to a more stable political settlement in the war-torn country. Russia, a key supporter of President Bashar al-Assad, has played a significant role in the conflict and in establishing safe zones across Syria. These zones, created in collaboration with Iran and Turkey, have helped reduce violence in certain areas, but conflict continues in other parts of the country, including ongoing efforts to combat jihadist groups. Despite these challenges, de Mistura remains optimistic about convening new talks in Geneva in the near future, with the fate of Assad remaining a key point of contention. This ongoing diplomatic effort holds the potential to bring much-needed peace and stability to Syria.

Premier Gladys Berejiklian's recent actions have been viewed as a clear indication that her government is not exempting affluent Liberal strongholds from the trend of privatizing public services. The decision to franchise Sydney's ferry system was followed by a contentious announcement from Transport Minister Andrew Constance regarding the privatization of buses in the inner west, mirroring the prevailing model in western Sydney. As tensions escalated, Berejiklian's presence at the Sydney Institute of Marine Science underscored her commitment to the matter. In the midst of this upheaval, Constance's unveiling of the new "B-Line" bus service for the lower north shore and northern beaches, to be managed by the government-operated State Transit, added another layer of complexity to the debate. When pressed on the potential extension of privatization to other affluent areas, Berejiklian remained noncommittal, stating, "I don't want to rule anything in or out at this stage."

The results of a global study have revealed that simply vacuuming and scrubbing the floor can provide enough exercise to protect your heart and increase your lifespan. According to scientists, just 30 minutes of activity per day, or 150 minutes per week, can significantly reduce the risk of death from any cause by 28 per cent and lower rates of heart disease by a fifth. The researchers, writing in The Lancet journal, emphasized that intense workouts or fancy gym memberships were not necessary for these health benefits. Surprisingly, only a small percentage of the over 130,000 participants in 17 countries who engaged in high levels of activity did so through traditional leisure activities, with the majority attributing their activity levels to commuting, physical jobs, or household chores.

Two months have passed since the ominous discovery of the Heartbleed bug, and yet the haunting specter of vulnerability still lingers over at least 300,000 servers. Like a relentless force of nature, this insidious bug, unearthed by a Google engineer, unleashed a frenzy of panic and a feverish frenzy of patching across the global web. Its venomous sting targets OpenSSL, a vital conduit for encrypting sensitive information, leaving accounts and passwords perilously exposed. What sets this bug apart is its nefarious entrenchment within the very framework of OpenSSL, leaving a staggering number of servers vulnerable to its malevolent grasp. Despite valiant efforts to stem the tide, the patch rate has dwindled to a mere trickle, leaving over 300,000 servers at the mercy of this relentless threat. As the dust settles, the grim reality emerges: the smaller entities may never find the resolve to shield themselves from this looming danger, leaving a trail of vulnerable systems in their wake. The ominous prophecy of security researcher Robert David Graham looms large, painting a grim picture of a future plagued by thousands of still-vulnerable systems, including those of critical significance. For those haunted by the specter of compromised accounts, a beacon of hope emerges in the form of McAfee's free checker, a lifeline for those seeking refuge in the tumultuous sea of cyber vulnerability.

Amid a recent surge in performance and playoff hopes, the Toronto Blue Jays are reportedly considering their options for next season. According to Bob Elliott of the Toronto Sun, the Blue Jays have reached out to former Detroit Tigers general manager Dave Dombrowski regarding the team's upcoming vacancy for president. After nearly 40 years with the organization, current president Paul Beeston is set to retire at the end of the season. Other notable candidates rumored to be interested in the position include Dan Duquette of the Baltimore Orioles and Kenny Williams of the Chicago White Sox. Dombrowski, 59, recently parted ways with the Tigers after over a decade with the team to explore new career opportunities, as announced by Tigers owner Mike Ilitch.

In a recent development, it has been revealed that Wolves president of operations, Flip Saunders, has engaged in discussions with the Celtics regarding Garnett. The details of who initiated these talks and the level of interest the Celtics have in players from the Wolves roster remain shrouded in mystery. Additionally, the question of whether Garnett would be willing to waive his no-trade clause to return to Minnesota adds another layer of uncertainty to the situation. It is unclear what the future holds for Garnett and the Wolves, especially with the ongoing negotiations with restricted free agent center, Pekovic. While the possibility of Garnett and Pekovic playing alongside each other is not out of the realm of possibility, it seems that Garnett is being considered more as a backup plan by Saunders. The emotional weight of these discussions and the unknown future add a sense of anticipation and intrigue to the narrative.

Existing research in economics has long touted the benefits of performance-based pay for increasing productivity. However, a contrasting perspective from the field of psychology suggests that such financial incentives may actually stifle creativity and innovation. In a recent study conducted in a controlled laboratory setting, it was found that a combination of allowing for early failures and rewarding long-term success proved to be the most effective strategy for motivating innovation. Participants under this incentive structure were more likely to explore new ideas and ultimately discover innovative business strategies compared to those under fixed-wage or traditional pay-for-performance schemes. Additionally, the study uncovered that the fear of termination could have a detrimental impact on innovation, while the presence of golden parachutes could mitigate these negative effects. These findings highlight the importance of carefully designing incentives to foster creativity and innovation within organizations.

A British man, Mounir Rarmoul-Bouhadjar, has pleaded guilty to possessing a bomb-making document found on a memory card, as reported after the lifting of reporting restrictions at the Old Bailey. Alongside him, Erol Incedal faces terrorism-related charges and is set to stand trial next week. The 26-year-old Rarmoul-Bouhadjar was acquitted of possessing an improperly obtained passport, with sentencing to follow at a later date. Initially identified as CD, Rarmoul-Bouhadjar and Mr Incedal, known as AB, were previously shielded from public identification under an order that has since been lifted. Despite efforts to conduct the trial entirely in private on grounds of national security, the Court of Appeal ruled that certain portions of the proceedings must be held in public. This development follows a challenge by media organizations against the unprecedented decision by Mr Justice Nicol to keep the trial completely confidential.

In the bustling city of Danang, Vietnam, amidst the sweltering heat and vibrant street markets, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau finds himself grappling with a contentious issue back home in Canada. The air is thick with tension as Trudeau addresses the looming shadow of Quebec's Bill 62, a divisive law that has stirred controversy nationwide. Against a backdrop of colorful silk lanterns and the tantalizing aroma of street food, Trudeau's words carry weight as he navigates the delicate balance between upholding the values of inclusivity and addressing concerns of security. The Prime Minister's stance, articulated with a mix of determination and diplomacy, resonates in the humid air, hinting at the complexities of governance in a multicultural society. As he contemplates the federal government's potential intervention, the echoes of dissent and advocacy reverberate through the bustling streets, underscoring the profound impact of this ongoing debate on the fabric of Canadian society.

Beneath the whispering winds of St James' Park, a dance of fate unfolds. Newcastle United, like a phoenix rising, have crafted a tapestry of hope in their pursuit of Lille's shining star, Mathieu Debuchy. The celestial symphony of negotiations swirls in the air, a delicate balance of desire and determination. With each heartbeat of the transfer window, the Magpies' resolve grows stronger, their fervor burning brighter. Like a comet streaking across the night sky, Debuchy's path to Newcastle seems written in the constellations, guided by the hand of destiny. As the echoes of Cabaye's longing reverberate through the cosmos, the stage is set for a celestial union, where footballing dreams take flight on wings of passion. In this celestial ballet, Debuchy's destiny awaits in the hallowed grounds of St James' Park, where the stars align in a shimmering embrace of possibility.

As BlackBerry forges ahead with its ambitious turnaround strategy, our unwavering focus remains on streamlining operations and maximizing productivity on a global scale. This entails a relentless pursuit of innovative methods to harness growth opportunities, all the while striving for sustainable profitability across every facet of our enterprise. Regrettably, this endeavor has necessitated the departure of a select number of employees in both Waterloo and Sunrise, FL. However, it is important to underscore that BlackBerry is actively seeking out new talent to spearhead our expansion in these areas. We extend our heartfelt gratitude to those individuals who have dedicated their efforts to the company, and we acknowledge their invaluable contributions. The recent workforce reductions were not unforeseen, especially in light of the company's shift towards the Android operating system from its former BB10 platform. It is important to note that, contrary to Mobile Syrup's initial report, BlackBerry has clarified that the total number of employees affected from both Waterloo and Sunrise is only approximately 200. Notably among them is the departure of BBM co-founder Gary Klassen.

Exciting news for tech-savvy families and entertainment enthusiasts alike, as Google unveils an impressive array of additions to their Chromecast app line-up. With a focus on family-friendly fun, the latest offerings include beloved classics like Wheel of Fortune, Scrabble Blitz, and Monopoly Dash. But the entertainment doesn't stop there – dance and trivia games like Big Web Quiz are also on the menu, promising hours of interactive enjoyment for players of all ages.

What sets these games apart is the seamless integration with Google's Knowledge Graph, ensuring that questions are always fresh and engaging. And with the ability to download apps from Google Play or the iOS App Store, players can use their phones and tablets as controllers, eliminating the need for cumbersome peripherals and streamlining the gaming experience. The game board itself will be displayed on the TV screen, creating an immersive and interactive experience for all involved.

For those who prefer a more laid-back form of entertainment, Google has also added two new entertainment channels to the Chromecast lineup – Showtime Anytime and Starz. With a wealth of TV shows and movies at your fingertips, there's never a dull moment when you're in front of the TV.

And if that wasn't enough to entice you, Google is sweetening the deal with two months of free Hulu Plus and 90 days of Google Play All Access Music for all Chromecast users. With so much to offer, it's clear that Google is pulling out all the stops to ensure that Chromecast remains at the forefront of home entertainment technology. Get ready to immerse yourself in a world of endless entertainment possibilities – the future of gaming and streaming has arrived.

Tragedy struck near the heart of Belgium as a train derailed and a carriage careened off the tracks, claiming the life of at least one person and leaving around 20 others wounded. The haunting scene unfolded as the train was departing from Leuven station, inching towards the bustling capital of Brussels. The sheer force of the derailment caused the carriage to topple onto its side, coming to a rest partway down a steep slope. The harrowing image of the damaged carriage, captured by AFP, serves as a stark reminder of the chaos and devastation that unfolded. As emergency services swiftly descended upon the crash site, the gravity of the situation became all too apparent. The suspension of services between Leuven and Brussels only added to the sense of despair and disruption. This tragic incident is not the first of its kind in Belgium, with previous train crashes in Hermalle-sous-Huy and Halle leaving a trail of heartbreak and sorrow in their wake. The scars of these past tragedies serve as a poignant reminder of the fragility of life and the enduring impact of such catastrophic events.

In the realm of cognitive enhancement, a beacon of hope emerges from the verdant world of antioxidant-rich plants, where the humble ginger root, known scientifically as Zingiber officinale, beckons with promises of heightened mental acuity. In a quest to unravel the mysteries of cognitive function, a group of intrepid researchers set out to explore the effects of this botanical elixir on the minds of middle-aged women, whose cognitive faculties stood at a crossroads. Through a meticulously designed study, sixty brave souls were enlisted to partake in this scientific odyssey, embarking on a journey of discovery that would test the limits of their cognitive prowess. As the days turned into weeks and the weeks into months, the participants were subjected to a battery of tests, their minds scrutinized with the precision of a watchmaker's eye. And lo, the results spoke volumes - the ginger-treated cohorts exhibited a remarkable reduction in P300 latencies, a surge in N100 and P300 amplitudes, and a palpable enhancement in working memory. Thus, a whisper of possibility lingered in the air, hinting at the transformative power of ginger as a potent ally in the quest for cognitive rejuvenation.

In a landmark decision, Spain has legalized a medication containing cannabis for the treatment of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) patients. The innovative tongue spray, known as Sativex, has been shown to effectively alleviate muscle spasms in individuals with MS who have not responded to traditional pain relievers. This groundbreaking development comes after the British pharmaceutical company, GW Pharmaceuticals, was granted permission to distribute the drug in the UK and has now secured approval in Spain through a partnership with Almirall. With sights set on wider European distribution, marketers are aiming to garner support from countries such as France, Germany, and Italy. As the Spanish Ministry of Health moves forward, pricing approval for Sativex is anticipated by year's end. Health Minister Trinidad Jimenez has emphasized the cautious prescription of the drug, while also clarifying that cannabis will not be utilized for the treatment of other diseases, such as cancer.

A recent poll conducted by the Rail, Tram and Bus Union paints a bleak picture of the mood among frontline public transport staff in NSW. According to the survey, a significant portion of bus and rail workers believe that the quality of public transport in the state has worsened over the past four years, with only a small percentage noting any improvement. While some acknowledge that services have been restored, concerns about security and the closure of ticket seller positions loom large. The survey results also highlight a lack of confidence in management, with the majority of staff expressing skepticism towards organizational changes. This data suggests a deep-seated discontent within the public transport workforce, signaling potential challenges for the future of the industry.

In the bustling city of Beijing, tensions were rising as LinkedIn found itself in hot water for bowing to the demands of Chinese censorship. The once popular professional networking site was facing backlash for censoring content deemed too sensitive by the Chinese government for seven long months. However, in a surprising turn of events, LinkedIn executives admitted that they may have been too quick to comply with China's strict censorship rules. 

As murmurs of discontent spread, LinkedIn executives found themselves at a crossroads, torn between their desire to expand their reach in China and their commitment to upholding freedom of expression. Hani Durzy, a spokesman for the California-based company, acknowledged the need for a change in policy. "We do want to get this right," he said, "and we are strongly considering changing our policy so that content from our Chinese members that is not allowed in China will still be viewed globally."

The decision to reconsider their stance on censorship marked a significant shift in LinkedIn's approach to doing business in China. The company's willingness to challenge China's aggressive censorship policies set them apart from other tech giants like Facebook, Twitter, and Google, who had long been blocked in the country. As LinkedIn grappled with the moral complexities of operating in a country known for its internet restrictions, the world watched with bated breath to see how this high-stakes game of cat and mouse would unfold.

The enigmatic disappearance of Serbian war crimes suspect Ratko Mladic has left his family in a state of uncertainty and despair. For nearly seven years, they have been shrouded in silence, with no word from the man accused of heinous acts against humanity. Now, as a last resort, the Mladic family has taken the heartbreaking step of filing a request for him to be declared legally dead. Their lawyer, Milos Saljic, revealed that the decision was made due to the family's complete lack of contact with Mladic and his deteriorating health. This tragic turn of events only adds to the weight of Mladic's indictment for genocide, a haunting legacy that continues to cast a dark shadow over the region. For the European Union, his capture remains a crucial demand for Serbia's future, further intensifying the urgency and gravity of Mladic's disappearance.

Reports from Chinese media have revealed a scene of chaos and fear as cracks snake their way across the U-shaped, glass-bottomed skywalk that winds around the rugged cliffs of Yuntai Mountain. Tourists, drawn to the vertiginous heights, fled in terror as the once pristine glass began to fracture beneath their feet, leaving a web of fissures in its wake. Suspended more than 1,000 meters above the earth, the skywalk had beckoned adventurers with its promise of a breathtaking view, but now it bore the scars of negligence and subpar craftsmanship. Photos circulated online, capturing the shattered tranquility of the structure, igniting a fervor of outrage among internet denizens. They decried the use of inferior materials in its construction, a betrayal of trust in the pursuit of profit. Officials, however, offered a different explanation. They pointed to the actions of careless tourists, who, in a moment of thoughtless abandon, had sent a thermos flask plummeting to the glass floor, triggering the fractures that now marred the once pristine surface. A spectacle of beauty and awe had been shattered, leaving behind a trail of shattered glass and shattered dreams.

In the bustling city of Bangkok, the United Nations has issued a stern call to Philippine authorities to launch a thorough investigation into President Rodrigo Duterte following his alarming confession of committing murder. Zeid Raad al-Hussein, the UN's High Commissioner for Human Rights, has shed light on the chilling reality of an "appalling epidemic of extra-judicial killings" unleashed by Duterte's ruthless war on drugs, claiming the lives of nearly 6000 individuals. In a bold move rarely seen from the international organization, Prince Zeid has denounced the shocking violence that has even targeted innocent children as young as five, expressing disbelief at the lack of accountability for such atrocities. Emphasizing the urgent need for justice, Prince Zeid has demanded that those responsible for the bloodshed be held accountable, sending a powerful message that no one, not even a national leader, is exempt from the rule of law.

Earlier this week, we reported on the efforts of an Indiana state legislator who sought to introduce creationism into the state's science classrooms. Despite managing to pass a modified bill that was less sectarian but still promoted religion, the leader of the Indiana House expressed concerns about the unconstitutional promotion of religion as determined by the Supreme Court. Many similar bills are introduced in state legislatures each year, often revealing a lack of understanding of both science and the law by their sponsors. In terms of science, misconceptions about the term "theory," the existence of multiple scientific explanations for life's diversity, and confusion regarding evolution as a theory for life's origin are common. Dennis Kruse, the sponsor of the Indiana bill, appears to exhibit these misunderstandings. On the legal front, many sponsors of such bills seem unaware of legal precedents, including Supreme Court decisions, that have ruled teaching creationism unconstitutional. Kruse, however, is aware of these precedents and hopes his bill will provoke a lawsuit that could lead the Supreme Court to overturn its own decisions. The House Speaker has indicated reluctance to challenge Supreme Court decisions, suggesting he will not bring the bill up for a vote. ScienceInsider has suggested that national media attention has made the bill politically toxic, highlighting the potential impact of continued coverage in promoting accurate science education.

That concludes our coverage of Uganda's presidential and parliamentary elections for today. The delayed start of voting in some areas was criticized by the leader of the Commonwealth observer mission, ex-Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, as "absolutely inexcusable". Criticism also arose due to the blocking of access to certain social media sites during the voting process, which President Yoweri Museveni attributed to security concerns. Opposition candidate Kizza Beisgye's temporary detention, the second instance within a week, was another notable event. Despite these challenges, many Ugandans expressed enthusiasm for the election, sharing photos of their inked thumbs on social media. The election results are expected to be announced by Saturday. The image of people in Kampala continuing to queue at a polling station at sunset captures the dedication of voters in this election.

Earlier today, Jovani "Fabbbyyy" Guillen announced his intention to join a new team and is currently considering offers from the North American League Championship Series or North American Challenger Series. With Phil "Jynthe" Vu set to start for Team Liquid in the North American Regional Finals against Team Envy this Saturday, it seems that this marks the end of Fabbbyyy's time with Team Liquid. Fabbbyyy, who replaced the longtime starting AD Chae "Piglet" Gwang-jin during the season, had a mixed rookie split with the club. He struggled in the playoffs against Counter Logic Gaming and was even subbed out in the series, being replaced by Jynthe, a player with no previous professional experience. Despite a 3-1 series loss, Jynthe outperformed Fabbbyyy in the two games he played, even contributing to TL's sole map victory in the third set. This transition marks a significant change for both Fabbbyyy and Team Liquid.

French media are abuzz with reports of a miraculous event that unfolded on a bustling Parisian street corner. An 18-month-old infant, left unattended by his parents, tumbled from a sixth-floor apartment, his tiny body descending through the air with alarming speed. But just as it seemed all hope was lost, a sharp-eyed doctor happened to be passing by, his trained instincts kicking in as he reached out to catch the falling child. The baby, a boy as it was later revealed, miraculously escaped unscathed as he bounced off the awning of a café below. The scene was a chaotic whirlwind of emotions as witnesses recounted the heart-stopping moment when the doctor's arms became the boy's last line of defense against the hard pavement below. The bustling intersection of Cours de Vincennes and Rue des Pyrenees in the 20th arrondissement bore witness to this breathtaking spectacle, as onlookers held their breath and prayed for a happy ending. The doctor, identified as Philippe Benseniot, later humbly declared that it was sheer luck that placed him in the right place at the right time. The baby's cries, initially piercing the air with fear, soon faded into a hushed calm as he was whisked away to the hospital for a thorough check-up. The streets of Paris whispered tales of this extraordinary event, where a brush with tragedy was averted by a split-second decision and a stroke of luck.

In the quaint village of Homberg in Hesse state, Germany, a tragic event unfolded that shook the community to its core. A simmering family feud erupted into a devastating explosion that left a trail of destruction in its wake. The 49-year-old man, consumed by anger and blinded by rage, made a fateful decision to unleash chaos upon his own home. After a heated argument that left emotions raw and tensions high, he retreated to his car only to return with a deadly arsenal of explosives. The deafening blast that followed not only claimed his own life but also left seven individuals wounded, their bodies battered by shrapnel and their spirits shattered by the senseless violence. Among the injured were family members, neighbors, and even brave police officers who had been called to intervene in the escalating conflict. As the smoke cleared and the dust settled, the once peaceful neighborhood now bore the scars of destruction, with shattered windows and crumbling walls bearing witness to the tragedy that had unfolded. In the aftermath of the explosion, the tight-knit community grappled with shock and disbelief, struggling to make sense of the senseless act that had torn apart their tranquil existence. As the authorities delved into the investigation, the identity of the bomber remained shrouded in secrecy, his name withheld in accordance with the strict privacy laws of Germany. With hearts heavy and minds reeling, the residents of Homberg were left to grapple with the harsh reality of how quickly life can be shattered by the explosive power of anger and resentment.

Established in 1713 by the compassionate Mary Chapman, the Bethel Hospital stands as a haunting relic of a bygone era. Despite its noble intention of providing humane treatment, the inventory reveals a harrowing truth - straight jackets, handcuffs, and padlocks were employed within its walls. While one third of the inmates were said to have left cured in the 19th century, a staggering number never left at all, succumbing to the confines of the institution. As the decades passed, the hospital gradually fell into disuse, with parts of the site closing in the 1970s and the entire facility shuttered by 1995. While most of the site underwent redevelopment, a small, eerie remnant remains to this day, a silent witness to the tragedies that unfolded within its walls. The history of the Bethel Hospital is a sobering reminder of the past, a poignant testament to the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

In a court of law, Mohammad Ali Mayat Baloch stood, his spirit unbroken despite the weight of his charges. With a heart full of love for the New Zealand Police, he found himself tangled in a web of misused telephones and late-night confessions fueled by alcohol's courage. Baloch's words, like poetry in the night, flowed freely as he showered the emergency services with praise and laughter, his jokes a beacon of light in the darkness. But one fateful night, a request for his address shattered the illusion of camaraderie, leading to his inevitable downfall. Yet, even in the face of adversity, Baloch remained unwavering in his admiration for the law, a sentiment instilled in him by his upbringing in a military family in Pakistan. As he awaited his fate, he clung to the hope that his positivity and genuine respect would be his salvation, a testament to the power of love even in the most unlikely of circumstances.

During a home affairs select committee hearing in the UK, Anthony House, a senior manager for public policy and communications at Google, emphasized the importance of not only removing harmful content online but also ensuring that individuals can access reliable and positive information. House highlighted the need for online platforms to provide a sense of community and hope for individuals who may be feeling isolated. In response to concerns about radicalization, Google has committed to enhancing the visibility of counter-radicalization videos on YouTube. This initiative comes after a recent meeting between government officials and leading tech companies in Silicon Valley to address the digital presence of extremist groups such as ISIS. Facebook has also expressed its intention to utilize its system for flagging suicidal users to identify individuals displaying signs of radicalization.

DeAndre Levy has dedicated his time and efforts in recent months to advocate against domestic violence and sexual assault. Now, the Detroit Lions linebacker is taking action by partnering with the Detroit Hustles Harder clothing line to launch a campaign selling "Our Issue" T-shirts. All proceeds from the shirts will benefit the Enough SAID program in Detroit, a collaborative effort between various organizations and the Wayne County Prosecutor's Office. The program aims to secure justice and closure for victims by testing over 11,000 unprocessed rape kits, investigating the crimes, and prosecuting the resulting cases. Levy's commitment to this cause was evident earlier this year when he penned a compelling essay on The Players Tribune, urging fellow athletes to speak out against sexual assault and domestic violence. His outspoken nature extends beyond this issue, as he has also been a vocal advocate for addressing brain trauma research in the NFL and supporting Colin Kaepernick's protest against racial inequality. Troy Vincent, the NFL Executive Vice President of Football Operations, recently commended Levy for his tireless efforts to combat domestic violence and sexual assault. Levy's unwavering dedication to creating a safer and more just community is truly commendable.

Earlier this year, Facebook embarked on a crusade against the insidious proliferation of fake news, implementing measures to distinguish reputable sources from dubious sources. In a bold move, the social media giant began to relegate content shared by prolific posters who inundate feeds with over 50 daily updates, as studies revealed a correlation between excessive posting and the dissemination of misinformation and sensationalism. Furthermore, Facebook took a decisive stand by providing fact-checkers' evaluations on potentially false articles, facilitating access to a plethora of related content for users seeking clarity. By prohibiting fake news websites from profiting through advertising on its platform and thwarting the dissemination of deceptive stories through targeted ad blocks, Facebook is intensifying its efforts to combat the dissemination of falsehoods. The latest update signifies a steadfast commitment to dismantling the economic incentives that fuel the propagation of fake news, a crucial step towards fostering a well-informed and discerning community within the realm of social media.

A procession of numerous Colombian farmers paraded through the bustling streets of Bogota, their fervent voices rising in unison to demand the government's adherence to accords forged in September. Leaders of the agrarian community lamented that the Colombian government had transgressed on 72 out of 88 meticulously hashed-out provisions, thus reigniting the flames of discontent that had simmered in the wake of previous protests. "The current state of affairs is either stagnant or, in some cases, deteriorating," asserted Cesar Pachon, a prominent figure among the farmers. In a previous outcry in August, these farmers had decried the government's agricultural policies as the harbingers of financial ruin, citing the inundation of the market with imported agricultural goods at prices unattainable to local producers. Compounded by escalating fuel and production costs, the once-thriving landscape of small-scale farming had metamorphosed into a landscape of unprofitability. Despite the government's subsequent pledges of ameliorative measures - such as fairer prices for agricultural commodities and enhanced access to credit facilities - to alleviate the plight of the farmers, Cesar Pachon, leading the Dignidades de Colombia movement, pronounced on a recent Tuesday that the beleaguered small-scale farmers were still compelled to sell their produce at a loss. The specter of imported goods continued to loom large, exacerbating the farmers' debts to financial institutions. In rebuttal, Colombia's Agriculture Minister, Ruben Dario Lizarralde, refuted claims of governmental noncompliance with the accords, asserting that the administration was earnestly endeavoring to fulfill the demands of the farming community. He avowed that extensive dialogues had been conducted with small-scale farmers to discern and address their pressing needs. In a demonstration of solidarity, healthcare workers joined the farmers in their march through the capital on Tuesday, expressing their own discontent with proposed alterations to the legislation governing social security.

Co-owner Chris Penny's dedication and skill as a barista at Sydenham cafe Hello Sunday was recognized with top honors at the Christchurch Hospitality Awards. The emotional impact of this achievement was felt deeply by Cantabrians, who passionately voted for their favorites in the industry. The sense of community and camaraderie was palpable as Dux Dine, Hello Sunday, and Baretta were celebrated for their excellence. The industry-run awards not only acknowledged the best in the business but also fostered a spirit of mutual appreciation among peers. The announcement of the winners at the awards ceremony on Sunday night was a moment of triumph and validation for all those who pour pints or craft flat whites. The accolades continued as Roots in Lyttelton was named Supreme Establishment of the Year, and Chef Giulio Sturla's innovative approach to local produce earned well-deserved acclaim. The emotional depth of the evening was further heightened as Boo Radleys and Three Boys Brewery were recognized for their excellence, showcasing the diversity and talent within the hospitality industry. For Hello Sunday, the emotional resonance of the evening was particularly profound as they not only took home the People's Choice Best Cafe award but also saw co-owner Chris Penny honored as Supreme Crew Member and Barista of the Year, a testament to his unwavering dedication and passion for his craft.

In a chilling twist of fate, a young British woman found herself face to face with her own mortality after a heart-wrenching fall from a horse left her with a broken neck. Thea Maxfield, just 26 years old, endured the unimaginable pain of a "hangman's fracture," a sharp and brutal break in her upper cervical vertebra. As she lay on the ground, her body trembling with shock, she realized the horrifying truth - her head was no longer connected to her body. With a courage born out of desperation, she gathered all her strength and lifted her fragile head back into place, her hands shaking with fear. The image of her cradling her own head in her hands is a haunting reminder of the fragility of life, a moment of raw vulnerability that will forever be etched in her memory. "I had to literally pick my head up and carry it in my hands," she whispered, her voice filled with disbelief. And in that moment, as she stared into the abyss of uncertainty, she knew that her journey towards healing would be a long and arduous one.

A group of fifteen radical Islamists has been apprehended in Moscow, with authorities seizing bombs, hand grenades, and firearms, according to Russian law enforcement. The individuals in question are reported to be affiliated with an Islamist organization known as At-Takfir Wal-Hijra. The arrests were carried out during early-morning raids at residences situated in the eastern part of the Russian capital. Law enforcement officials also discovered three improvised explosive devices, as well as the necessary components for constructing additional explosives. At-Takfir Wal-Hijra was formally outlawed by Russia's Supreme Court in 2010 on grounds of fomenting ethnic and religious discord, as detailed by the Interfax news agency. The group has been frequently cited in local media reports as a prominent extremist entity in the area, though any potential connection with a similarly-named militant group established in Egypt during the 1960s remains uncertain. The impending Winter Olympics set to be held in Sochi, a Black Sea resort in Russia, within a span of just over two months, will likely amplify the international scrutiny surrounding these arrests, observes BBC correspondent Daniel Sandford in Moscow. The ongoing conflict between Russian military forces and separatists in Chechnya has served to fuel extremist activities by Islamist factions, resulting in a spillover of violence throughout the North Caucasus, encompassing regions such as predominantly Muslim Ingushetia and Dagestan, claiming numerous casualties including government officials and security personnel. While the frequency of militant incidents in Moscow has diminished following the conclusion of Russia's second campaign in Chechnya, the gravity of attacks that have transpired, such as the suicide bombing at Domodedovo international airport in January 2011 claiming the lives of 37 individuals, underscores the persistent threat posed by extremist elements.

Many experienced IT professionals have grappled with the decision between freelancing and traditional employment. Freelancing allows for creative freedom but can be uncertain when it comes to income. Working for a larger company offers stability but often comes with limitations on creativity and personal expression. We are part of a movement of creative professionals seeking an alternative to the traditional business model. The worker-cooperative approach allows IT professionals to have control over their work and personal lives, produce high-quality work, and reap the benefits of their efforts without sacrificing security. Our tech cooperatives offer the support and collaboration of a traditional firm, but with the added bonus of being owned and governed democratically by the employees themselves. This panel discussion will offer firsthand accounts of working in tech cooperatives, exploring why more IT professionals are choosing this model, the pros and cons of a democratic workplace, and the steps involved in establishing and sustaining a worker cooperative.

Basho is boldly venturing into the realm of open-source with its latest initiative, unleashing Riak CS, a revolutionary storage software seamlessly integrated with Amazon Web Services. This groundbreaking technology will now be freely available under the esteemed Apache 2 license. This strategic move by Basho, renowned for its exceptional Riak distributed high-performance database, signifies a pivotal moment in the tech industry. Riak CS, built atop Riak's robust foundation, embodies the very essence of distributed systems, addressing the complex storage challenges faced by modern enterprises. Boasting a plethora of cutting-edge features, including fault-tolerant storage, support for massive objects, S3-compatible API, and sophisticated authentication mechanisms, Riak CS promises a transformative storage solution for businesses of all sizes. Embracing an operational model for seamless scalability, as well as a sleek visual interface for comprehensive monitoring and metrics, this software is set to revolutionize the way companies manage their data. By open-sourcing Riak CS, Basho not only asserts its commitment to innovation but also paves the way for further collaborations with the global open-source community. This strategic move allows Basho to focus on enhancing its proprietary Riak Enterprise while nurturing a vibrant ecosystem of developers dedicated to refining and expanding the capabilities of Riak CS. In an era where data sovereignty and seamless data transfer are paramount, Riak CS emerges as a game-changer, designed to effortlessly handle files up to 5 gigabytes and beyond. As the industry shifts towards a hybrid cloud approach, with public data centers offering cost-effective storage solutions and private data centers safeguarding critical enterprise data, the demand for versatile storage software is at an all-time high. The rise of open-source initiatives such as Cloudstack and OpenStack further underscores the significance of Basho's decision to open-source Riak CS, aligning perfectly with the evolving needs of the market. With its unwavering commitment to open-source values, Basho is poised to capitalize on the burgeoning demand for flexible storage solutions that transcend traditional boundaries, driving innovation and empowering businesses to thrive in the digital age.

Network Rail has issued a warning to residents to secure garden furniture in preparation for Storm Brian, which is set to impact parts of the UK and the Republic of Ireland this weekend. The Met Office has issued a "yellow" warning for parts of Britain on Saturday, indicating possible travel disruptions. Network Rail, in collaboration with train operators, has activated weather contingency plans for certain routes and advises passengers to anticipate potential travel disruptions. These contingencies may include temporary speed restrictions due to high winds, which could cause debris to be blown onto railway tracks and overhead power lines. In related news, the M40 was temporarily closed on Friday night following a road incident involving a lorry and several vehicles. Officials are working diligently to repair emergency barriers damaged in the crash, resulting in significant delays for drivers. Network Rail is urging residents living near railway tracks to secure garden furniture, equipment, and trampolines to prevent them from being blown onto the tracks or overhead power lines. A spokesperson for Network Rail emphasized the organization's vigilance and preparation for severe weather conditions.

Iran and Russia have engaged in discussions regarding a draft agreement to construct a minimum of two nuclear power plants within the Islamic Republic, as reported by Iran's official news agency. During the visit of Russian official Nikolai Spassky, an initial agreement was reached on Wednesday between Russian and Iranian nuclear officials concerning the proposed facilities, as detailed by IRNA. Behrouz Kamalvandi, spokesman for the Iranian Atomic Energy Organisation, confirmed the preliminary agreement, stating that the construction of two new 1,000 megawatt plants is planned to take place alongside the existing power station in Bushehr, which was also developed by Russia. Further discussions will focus on technical and financial aspects of the project, with a final agreement anticipated to be signed in the near future. The Bushehr facility has been operational since 2011 with a capacity of 1,000 megawatts. Despite enduring stringent Western sanctions on its oil and banking sectors, Iran is expected to finance the new Bushehr project through a barter arrangement. Tehran's ambassador to Russia, Mehdi Sanaei, disclosed last month that negotiations between the two nations involve Iran supplying hundreds of thousands of barrels of oil daily in exchange for Russian goods and services, including the proposed nuclear plants.

A myth, born in the digital ether of 2011, dances across the internet in a waltz of YouTube videos, blogs, and Tweets. During an unfortunate incident on Sunday, an Iraqi airport employee named Karim Obaid Bardan was tragically killed by US troops who mistakenly believed they were under attack. As Bardan approached a military convoy on his way to work, he disregarded repeated signals to slow down or turn on his headlights, causing the convoy to perceive his vehicle as a threat. In order to protect themselves and the convoy from a potential attack, the troops made the difficult decision to engage the vehicle with small-arms fire. It is important to note that Iraqi drivers are well aware of the need to exercise caution and refrain from any behavior that may be perceived as threatening when approaching military vehicles. This incident occurred just a day after Prime Minister Nouri al-Maliki declared that US troops would not be required in Iraq beyond the previously established December 2011 withdrawal deadline. An Iraqi policeman has confirmed that Bardan did not stop or slow down. Several Iraqi officials, speaking anonymously, have described the shooting as a mistake that took place near a security checkpoint on the road to the airport. The US military is currently conducting an investigation into the incident and deeply regrets the loss of Bardan's life. Meanwhile, in another part of Baghdad, a roadside bomb claimed the life of an innocent passer-by and injured three individuals, two of whom were policemen, during the busy morning rush hour.

The Australian government, under the leadership of the Turnbull administration, is taking decisive steps towards implementing export restrictions on liquefied natural gas producers. This strategic move is part of a concerted effort to safeguard domestic gas supply and mitigate price fluctuations. Resources Minister Matt Canavan will officially notify LNG producers of this development on Monday, signaling the activation of the Australian Domestic Gas Security Mechanism. This mechanism, introduced on July 1 as a cornerstone of the Coalition's comprehensive energy security strategy, empowers the government to assess and address potential gas shortages in the upcoming year. Through this mechanism, the government can exercise regulatory oversight over LNG projects that rely on domestic gas reserves, ensuring that sufficient supply is available to meet the needs of Australian consumers. Should the need arise, the government reserves the authority to impose restrictions on exports or mandate the sourcing of alternative gas supplies to maintain a stable and reliable energy market.

During a hearing by the National Assembly's Defense Committee, South Korean Defense Minister Kim Kwan-jin confirmed that North Korea's test launch of a KN-06 surface-to-air missile into the West Sea earlier this month was successful. The KN-06 was unveiled at a military parade in October 2015 and was officially verified in South Korea's 2010 Defense White Paper. The missile is capable of shooting down enemy fighters and is fired vertically toward a flying target, unlike previous North Korean missiles. It is similar to the Russian S-300 and has a range of up to 150 km. North Korea developed the KN-06 after facing difficulties in acquiring new fighter jets, while South Korea has been able to upgrade its fighter jets with the acquisition of F-15Ks.

The sun sets over the sprawling campus of Stellenbosch University in Cape Town, casting a warm glow over the historic buildings and tree-lined pathways. As students make their way to and from classes, a sense of anticipation and excitement fills the air. The university has undergone a transformation, adopting a new admissions policy for 2018 that aims to address past injustices and create a more inclusive environment.

In a statement released over the weekend, the university outlined its commitment to reserving places for socio-economically disadvantaged students, regardless of their racial background. This bold move is the result of years of consultations and investigations, culminating in a policy that seeks to prioritize academic merit, diversity, and redressing economic disparities.

As the campus buzzes with activity, the university's rector, Prof Wim de Villiers, stands tall and proud, declaring Stellenbosch a university for all South Africans. This declaration is a powerful statement in a country still grappling with the legacy of apartheid and striving towards a more equal society.

In the distance, the majestic mountains of Stellenbosch provide a breathtaking backdrop to this scene of progress and change. The university's new language policy, adopted last June, further demonstrates its commitment to accessibility and inclusivity, making provisions for students who prefer to study in Afrikaans while also improving access for English-speaking students.

Overall, Stellenbosch University is a beacon of hope and progress in South Africa, leading the way towards a more just and equitable society.

But the brave passengers and crew, guided by a primal instinct for survival, banded together to overpower the would-be hijackers.

UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon has expressed his intention to visit North Korea in the near future, although no final decision has been reached. This marks the first official acknowledgment of ongoing discussions regarding the potential visit. Recent reports suggesting a confirmed visit, including a meeting with leader Kim Jong-un this week, have been denied by the UN. The upcoming rare talks between North and South Korea on Thursday aim to improve relations following heightened tensions in August, when a brief exchange of fire occurred at the heavily guarded border. Despite North Korea's criticism of South Korea for a recent live-fire drill near their disputed sea border, Mr. Ban, a former South Korean foreign minister, has emphasized his willingness to play a constructive role in promoting peace, stability, and dialogue on the Korean Peninsula. While a planned visit to North Korea in May was abruptly cancelled, recent reports hint at positive developments regarding a potential future visit. Mr. Ban, if his visit proceeds, would become only the third UN chief to visit North Korea, a country facing UN sanctions due to its nuclear weapons program. As the two Koreas remain technically at war without a peace treaty signed after the 1950-1953 conflict, Mr. Ban's visit holds significance in the ongoing efforts towards peace and reconciliation in the region.

This initiative is a beacon of hope for the future of British tennis, and a chance for dreams to take flight.

Within the confines of the largest US prison in Afghanistan, a silent rebellion has taken root, gradually unfurling like a hidden flower in the shadows. For a fortnight now, the prisoners have chosen to remain ensconced within their cells, shunning the call of showers and the solace of exercise in a poignant protest against their indefinite captivity. This act of defiance, cloaked in the cloak of solitude, unveils a rare glimpse into the heart of Bagram - a place obscured from public scrutiny, its secrets veiled behind impenetrable walls. The whispers of discontent first surfaced on July 1, a clandestine murmur that grew louder with each passing day. The International Committee of the Red Cross, the silent observer in this unfolding drama, revealed the prisoners' plight to their families, a stark revelation of canceled video links and forsaken family visits. Yet, the inmates, like shadows in the night, refused to meet the gaze of their benevolent watchers. Hunger strikes and violence were not their chosen weapons; instead, they wielded the silence of solidarity, a steadfast refusal to bend to the will of their captors. Ramzi Kassem, the voice of the voiceless, spoke on behalf of a Yemeni prisoner, shedding light on their shared plight - an existence devoid of trial, devoid of legal recourse, suspended in a limbo of uncertainty. The US military, an enigmatic entity hovering on the fringes of this drama, remained cloaked in silence, an enigmatic specter observing from afar. Unlike Guantanamo Bay, where a glimmer of hope remains in the form of legal representation, the 620 souls confined within the walls of Bagram languish in isolation, cut off from the outside world. Afghan Government representatives, locked out of this fortress of despair, stand powerless, unable to breach the fortress walls that hold their fellow countrymen captive. And so, within the shadows of Bagram, a quiet storm rages on, a symphony of silence echoing through the corridors of confinement, a testament to the resilience of the human spirit in the face of adversity.

Tottenham Hotspur has recently announced the release of seven players, a decision that did not come as a surprise. Among those departing are Gomes, Giancarlo Gallifuoco, Cameron Lancaster, Roman Michael-Percil, Jonathan Miles, Kevin Stewart, and Lawrence Vigouroux. Gomes, the only senior player to be released, had his departure confirmed yesterday. Gallifuoco and Lancaster, once seen as potential Premier League talents, are now expected to pursue opportunities in lower league football with the goal of ascending the English football hierarchy once again. On the other hand, young players Dominic Ball, Grant Hall, Jon Obika, and Nathan Oduwa have had their contracts extended, indicating that the club sees potential for them in the Premier League or as valuable assets for future transfer deals. Notably, the Premier League retained and released list reveals that contract offers have been made to Brad Friedel and Souleymane Coulibaly. While their departure remains a possibility, the club is actively working to retain them. Additionally, new offers have also been extended to several academy players, including the highly regarded Harry Winks.

Get ready for an adventure with Team Kaylie as the selfie-obsessed socialite is forced to lead a wilderness club after one too many mishaps. Join lovable Charlie in his Colorforms City as he takes you on imaginative shape-filled story expeditions with a colorful cast of characters. Embark on magical missions with quick-witted YooHoo and his crew as they travel the globe to help animals in need. Discover the prequel to a fantasy classic in The Dark Crystal: Age of Resistance, where three young Gelfling inspire a rebellion against a cruel Emperor. Join astronaut Niko Breckenridge and her crew as they face unimaginable danger on a high-risk mission to explore the genesis of an alien artifact in Another Life. Finally, get ready for an epic battle as high schooler Daisuke and his friends are conscripted to fight a hostile cyborg race in revisions when Shibuya time-warps to 2388.

The Yarra River at Warrandyte weeps, tainted by toxic tears that flow from a concrete heart, where a dark secret lies hidden beneath the surface. A deadly cocktail of chemicals and herbicides dances with the water, poisoning the land and sky, creating a haunting melody of sorrow and despair. Trees bow their heads in mourning, their roots tangled in a toxic embrace, as the river whispers a tale of betrayal and loss. Siblings frolic in the tainted waters, unaware of the danger that lurks beneath the surface, their laughter mingling with the cries of the poisoned earth. In this tangled web of beauty and destruction, a fragile balance is broken, leaving a scar on the land that can never be erased.

An elite university in China has recently made the controversial decision to terminate the contract of Xia Yeliang, a prominent economist known for his advocacy for free speech. Reports indicate that the economics faculty at Peking University voted to expel him, highlighting the university's intolerance towards dissenting voices. Xia Yeliang's outspoken support for democratic values and involvement in drafting Charter 08, a manifesto advocating for political reform in China, has likely made him a target for China's increasingly authoritarian regime. The timing of his dismissal, amid a crackdown on media and internet freedom and the arrest of bloggers and activists, underscores the government's efforts to silence dissenting voices. Xia's close association with Liu Xiaobo, the Nobel Peace Prize winner who is currently imprisoned, further illustrates his commitment to advocating for political change in China. The international community, including organizations like the Committee of Concerned Scientists, has expressed concern over Xia's dismissal and called on Peking University to reconsider its decision. Xia Yeliang's experience serves as a stark reminder of the challenges faced by those who dare to speak out against the Chinese government's oppressive policies. His time as a visiting scholar at Stanford University in California further highlights the importance of academic freedom and the need to protect scholars who face persecution for their beliefs.

President Donald Trump's announcement on Thursday, regarding the United States' withdrawal from the Paris climate agreement, was a spectacle filled with conflicting emotions. As he stood in the White House Rose Garden, surrounded by administration officials and conservative supporters, the air was tense with anticipation. The sun beat down on the gathered crowd, casting harsh shadows on their faces as they listened to Trump's words. The gravity of the decision hung heavy in the air, contrasting starkly with the vibrant blooms of the garden surrounding them. Trump's voice echoed through the garden, his words a mix of defiance and determination as he spoke of protecting America and its citizens. The scene was a whirlwind of political theater, a clash of ideals and interests that left the world reeling in its wake.

Pope Francis has approved the canonization of five child saints: two Portuguese shepherd children who claimed to have seen the Virgin Mary in Fatima 100 years ago, and three Mexican adolescents who were martyred for their faith in the 16th century. Without the requirement of a miracle, Francis declared the three Child Martyrs of Tlaxcala as saints. The boys, Cristobal, Antonio, and Juan, were converted to Catholicism in the early 1500s. In contrast, Francis did approve a miracle for Francisco and Jacinta Marto, the Fatima siblings, just before his upcoming visit to the Fatima shrine to commemorate the centennial anniversary of their apparitions.

In the remote village of Latti, nestled in the rugged terrain of Afghanistan's Sar-e-Pul province, a tragic and senseless act of violence unfolded. A 30-year-old Afghan woman, whose name will forever be etched in the annals of injustice, was brutally beheaded by a group of Taliban militants. Her supposed crime? A mere act of independence - she dared to venture out for a simple shopping trip without the accompaniment of her husband. The dusty streets of Latti bore witness to the chilling scene as the armed men, cloaked in the shadows of their fundamentalist beliefs, mercilessly took her life.

As the sun dipped below the horizon and cast a haunting glow over the village, whispers of fear and disbelief spread like wildfire. The woman's husband, miles away in Iran, was unaware of the horrors unfolding in his absence. The Taliban, shrouded in denial and deceit, distanced themselves from the heinous act, washing their hands of blood that stained the village's already troubled history.

In a land where the rights of women are but a distant dream, where the echoes of oppression reverberate through the barren landscape, brave souls like Captain Niloofar Rahmani defy the odds. Rahmani, a trailblazer in a male-dominated domain, had soared through the skies as Afghanistan's first female fixed-wing pilot. But her wings were clipped by the looming shadows of terror and threats that loomed over her and her family. Seeking asylum in the United States, Rahmani faced a harsh backlash from her homeland, accused of betrayal and deceit by those who could not fathom the gravity of her fears.

In the midst of chaos and conflict, the story of the Afghan woman and Captain Niloofar Rahmani intertwine, painting a vivid portrait of courage and sacrifice in a land where freedom is a fragile dream. Their struggles, their defiance, and their unwavering spirit speak volumes about the resilience of the human spirit in the face of darkness. And as the world watches in horror, their voices echo through the windswept valleys of Afghanistan, calling for justice, for change, for a future where women can walk the streets without fear, and soar through the skies without restraint.

Canterbury legend and director Steve Mortimer is gripped by a sense of unease as he watches the Bulldogs struggle to maintain their identity under coach Des Hasler. The fear that they are "losing our DNA" looms large in Mortimer's mind as he prepares for a crucial meeting that could determine Hasler's future at the club. The once tight-knit "Family Club" now faces a crossroads, with several directors, including Mortimer, expressing concerns about the team's direction. As they prepare to convene for an emergency meeting on Friday, the tension in the air is palpable.

Hasler's future hangs in the balance, with negotiations for a contract extension at a standstill. If the decision is made to part ways with Hasler, the possibility of former Bulldogs player and Raiders assistant coach Dean Pay stepping in as head coach looms large. Mortimer, a revered figure at the club, finds himself torn between his respect for Hasler as a coach and his doubts about his ability to lead the Bulldogs to success.

The weight of the situation is heavy on Mortimer's shoulders as he grapples with the uncertainty and conflicting emotions swirling around him. The future of the Bulldogs hangs in the balance, and Mortimer must navigate the delicate balance between loyalty to the club's traditions and the need for change. As he enters the meeting room, Mortimer knows that the decisions made today will shape the fate of the club for years to come.

Once again, Austin Harig finds himself entangled in a legal web, his youthful bravado leading him down a path of conflict and confrontation. In the early hours of Thursday morning, the tranquility of Zittel Street in South Buffalo was shattered by a tumultuous altercation, leaving a young man with grave injuries on the porch stairs. It is a scene that speaks of reckless abandon and impulsive actions, a stark contrast to the hopeful young candidate who once dared to challenge the establishment in the 2016 Buffalo School Board election. As the dust settles, Harig and his companion, Jonathan Tyner, are led away in the custody of law enforcement, their futures marred by charges of assault and harassment. This unfortunate incident marks the second time this year that Harig has found himself in legal jeopardy, a troubling pattern that threatens to overshadow the potential he once held. It is a sobering reminder of the perils of youth and the consequences of misplaced choices.

Visiting the Videogame History Museum has been a challenge due to most of its collection being in storage and the limited availability of its cross-country tours. However, a recent approval from a Frisco, Texas community board means that the Museum will soon have a permanent public display at a 10,400 square foot location inside the city's Discovery Center by April. While this space may not be huge, it will allow visitors to easily revisit consoles that were significant in their youth. This location is just the beginning, as the founders plan to secure funding from corporate sponsors to establish a larger base of operations in the future. Although Frisco may not be easily accessible for those outside the Dallas area, it is a more reliable option than waiting for the nomadic exhibit to come to your city.

The events in Jerusalem and southern Israel have left a deep sense of fear and tension in the air. The tragic death of the man at the hands of soldiers, and the subsequent fatal shooting of the Eritrean migrant, have left an indelible mark on the collective consciousness. The heightened suspicions and violence have led to a palpable sense of unease, prompting many Israelis to seek out means of self-defense, such as pepper spray and firearms. These harrowing experiences have left a lasting impact, shaping the way people navigate their daily lives in this turbulent environment.

The International Space Station serves as a hub for advanced scientific research, yet it also provides a platform for astronauts to engage in recreational activities. In a recent feature, Mashable showcased a collection of captivating photographs captured by Chris Hadfield, the 53-year-old Canadian commander of the space station. These striking images, taken as the station orbits Earth, offer a unique perspective on our planet. Notable snapshots include a minuscule moonrise, a distinct demarcation between Israel and Egypt, an aerial view of Pyongyang, North Korea, and a mesmerizing early morning depiction of New York City, with the skyscrapers of downtown Manhattan casting an impressive shadow on the water. Hadfield's son Evan plays a pivotal role in promoting his father's remarkable photography, resulting in widespread online acclaim and a substantial following on Twitter, surpassing 650,000 followers. Furthermore, a recent video posted by Hadfield, illustrating the effects of crying in a zero-gravity environment, garnered significant attention. As Hadfield continues his orbit 230 miles above Earth until May, it is anticipated that he will continue to capture and share compelling imagery. For those interested in following Hadfield's journey and exploring more of his photographs, further information is available via the provided link.

The recent legalization of strip shows and wet t-shirt contests in Saskatchewan marks a significant shift in the province's historically strict liquor laws. While performers are still required to adhere to certain restrictions, such as covering their nipples and prohibiting full frontal nudity, the change has been welcomed by individuals like Anna Scott, the artistic director of the Bottoms Up Burlesque Club. Scott highlights the challenges her dancers faced under the previous regulations, where even minor actions like removing a glove or feather boa could be classified as strip-tease. With the new regulations in place, Scott anticipates an easier process for arranging shows at her club. However, the impact of this legal change on the broader entertainment industry remains uncertain. The decision to regulate adult entertainment in Saskatoon, limiting strip shows and wet t-shirt contests to specific zones, reflects a cautious approach by local authorities. Overall, the shift in liquor laws in Saskatchewan raises questions about the intersection of alcohol consumption and adult entertainment, and the potential implications for businesses and communities.

The Zatopek in Melbourne on Thursday night exudes tradition and history, but the 10,000-metre track race that it is named after may soon be erased from the Olympics. The IOC has made sweeping changes, putting five key events, including the 200-metre sprint and shot put, in jeopardy in order to make room for other sports in the Olympics schedule. It's a heartbreaking blow to the sport, as the 10,000 metres, one of the men's race walks, the 200, shot put, and triple jump are all at risk of being eliminated. The gravity of the situation was made clear at a meeting of influential figures in the sport, where these events were presented as the most obvious choices for changes. It's a devastating loss for the athletics community, and the impact of these potential changes cannot be understated.
